Optical skyrmions are topologically protected swirls of light polarization, promising for communication, storage, and particle manipulation. Reshaping them on demand, between Bloch-type, Néel-type, and intermediate textures, has been awkward with conventional optics.

The team sends vector vortex beams through an active mixture whose enantiomeric excess, the imbalance between mirror-image molecules, they control. Tuning that excess converts skyrmions reversibly between Bloch, Néel, and intermediate states, and the same trick transforms bimerons once a birefringent plate is added. The skyrmion number stays conserved, even for higher-order textures, showing the transformations are robust. The common-path setup is stable and cheap, needing fewer wave plates than rival schemes. Chemical tuning of light's topology offers a flexible platform for information processing with structured light.
arxiv-2606-15907:
Izmestiev and colleagues revisit the flexibility of discrete conjugate nets in 2026, polyhedral surfaces of quadrilateral faces arranged like a square grid. A generic such net is rigid: it admits no deformation beyond rigid motion. A published claim held that a non-degenerate net whose 3-by-3 subnets are all flexible must itself be flexible.

The claim, it turns out, is false as stated: the authors construct counterexamples. They then prove a corrected version under stronger side conditions, restoring the local-to-global implication where it belongs. Their global theorems extend to all simply connected nets, while nets with holes need different methods, illustrated through flexible tubes. The work has a mechanical echo: the nets correspond to parallel manipulators, where the same distinctions separate flexing mechanisms from first-order rigid ones.
arxiv-2606-16107:
Xu, Huang, and Wu tackle variable-rate image compression in 2026, where one model must serve many quality levels. Deep compression now beats traditional standards on quality, but changing the rate usually needs several networks or one complex model. Both options cost storage or computation. The authors borrow a fine-tuning trick from language models instead.

Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, tunes a model through small added matrices that later merge back into the weights. Their LoRA Rate-Adaptive Module, LoRAM, applies this idea progressively so one model can switch rates. Because the pieces merge back, they add no extra computation at use time in the design described. Variable-rate compression uses only 0.1 percent added parameters in the reported system. Tests verify LoRA-based adaptation works well for this task. One compact codec spanning rates could simplify streaming and medical imaging alike.
arxiv-2606-16207:
Abhishek and Mummidi build a neutrino model in 2026 where one symmetry pattern fixes the whole lepton flavor structure. Neutrinos have tiny masses and mix at large angles, facts the Standard Model alone cannot explain. Radiative models generate those masses through loops instead of a direct term. The scotogenic model is one such loop scheme, with dark sector particles in the loop.

Here the finite modular group S4 controls the flavor symmetry. All Yukawa couplings, the numbers setting masses and mixing, come from modular forms: functions of a single complex parameter, the modulus. One parameter thus replaces the usual flavon fields and their vacuum values. The scotogenic loop mechanism sits inside this modular frame. The combined model addresses neutrino masses, leptonic mixing, and the cosmic baryon asymmetry together, the last through flavored resonant leptogenesis. A scan over the modulus maps the viable space: fewer free inputs, sharper predictions.
arxiv-2606-16407:
Trinley and co-authors open the hood of language models in 2026 to find why they mishandle pronouns when several referents carry different ones. Behavioral tests alone cannot show which internal mechanism fails. The authors test three candidate mechanisms: group entity binding, which ties a pronoun to its referent group; recency bias, which favors the latest mention; and stereotypical bias, which follows social expectations. Using Boundless Distributed Alignment Search, they hunt for each mechanism inside the network.

All three turn up as separable causal subspaces spread across the network's depth. Together they account for 91 to 99.5 percent of model behavior on the task, per the report. Most models lean mainly on recency and stereotype, while group binding contributes little and sometimes adds noise. Attention analysis reveals two competing copying routes: a localized concept-level route shared by binding and stereotype, and a distributed token-level route used by recency.
arxiv-2606-16507:
Spindler and co-authors release in 2026 segmentation maps tracing the spiral arms and bars of 639,636 galaxies, drawn by a neural network taught by citizen scientists. The maps come from the DESI Legacy Survey imaging. A U-net-style network, dubbed ZooBot:3D, trains on pixel masks from the Galaxy Zoo: 3D project, where volunteers outlined galactic structures by hand. Its outputs are soft maps: each pixel carries the model's confidence that it lies in a spiral arm or a bar.

Within the catalogue, 512,216 galaxies show a high likelihood of spiral arms, and 230,511 a strong or weak bar, per the survey classifications. The model also shows an emergent knack for finding rings, although ring galaxies were scarce in its training data. Cross-matched subsamples tie the maps to the MaNGA and SAMI spectroscopic surveys, with about 29,000 and 5,000 objects respectively. The full dataset is public.
arxiv-2606-16707:
Li argues in a 2026 paper that a personal AI agent should store its memory of the user as running code. Today's agents keep memory as loose text, a graph, or a flat list of facts, then fetch whichever entries look similar to a new request. That style recalls single facts well, but handles contradictions, totals and hard rules poorly.

The proposal, User as Code, models the user as a living software project. Typed Python objects hold the user's state, and ordinary functions encode the rules that govern it, so storage and reasoning share one runnable medium. A two-phase pipeline first logs every fact without discarding anything, then periodically checkpoints the log into clean structured code. On a standard long-conversation benchmark, recall matches the best prior systems. On aggregate questions, like counting last year's trips, retrieval memory collapses while code-based memory holds up.
arxiv-2606-16807:
Pirlogeanu and colleagues link spoken words to written words through images in a 2026 speech technology paper. Many languages lack transcripts, so training speech systems the usual way is impossible or costly. Pictures with spoken descriptions can be gathered anywhere, though, even where literacy is low.

Their method starts from image captions written by captioning systems, giving a vocabulary of visible concepts. For each written word, they gather utterances whose pictures were captioned with that word. An unsupervised word discovery step then aligns those utterances to locate the spoken segment matching the word. No text supervision is used at any point. In retrieval and keyword spotting tests, the approach beats a strong neural baseline while staying easier to interpret. A continuous-feature version scores best overall, while a discrete version runs more cheaply. The English proof of concept motivates work on low-resource languages without written records.
arxiv-2606-16907:
Yanda Tao and colleagues present Tangram in a 2026 systems paper on training large language models over mixed GPU clusters. Real clusters grow over time, so they mix graphics processor types with different speeds, memory and links. Automatic parallelizers that split models across devices face an exploding search space on such mixed hardware, and they often drop useful parallelism modes to cope.

Tangram hides the mixture from the planner. Profiling finds homogeneous islands, groups of similar devices bought together. The model is cut into slices, each slice is planned by an existing homogeneous parallelizer on one island, and the slices are composed into balanced pipelines. A narrow interface connects Tangram to existing tools, and heterogeneity-guided pruning speeds the search by about an order of magnitude. Measured training throughput beats current heterogeneous parallelizers by more than a factor of two at best, while matching homogeneous tools on uniform clusters.
arxiv-2606-17107:
Li reframes a language model's key-value cache as a notebook in a 2026 inference paper. Prefix caching reuses computation only for an exact shared prefix; changing one field invalidates everything after it. Patching the field's cached vectors fails: the model keeps acting on the old value.

Experiments across four model families show why: during prefill, the model writes conclusions conditioned on that field onto downstream tokens, its notes. The field's own vectors drive under one percent of the decision. Two capabilities follow. The cache is editable: append a salient erratum and the notes amend themselves, at a tiny fraction of recompute cost. It is also composable: notes are portable, so a precompiled skill can be spliced into a new context, matching full recomputation. In an online serving benchmark, the trick keeps cache hit rates high and slashes time to first token.
arxiv-2606-17207:
Antoci and colleagues present a 2026 arXiv paper on a puzzling class of pulsating stars. They call them wildly oscillating stars, or WOS for short. Space telescopes show dense, ridge-like clusters of frequencies in some A and F type stars. The clusters sit below the fundamental radial mode, where classical theory expects none.

The team analysed Kepler and TESS photometry and built frequency diagrams. Rotation, binarity, and standard excitation models were all tested as explanations. The effect appears only where two known instability strips overlap on the diagram. In at least two stars, many peaks are nonlinear combination frequencies of other modes. Yet the parent modes must sit inside the cluster itself, so current models still miss the cause.
arxiv-2606-17407:
Zhang and colleagues present a 2026 arXiv paper on light-like waves in a honeycomb array of microcavity pillars holding exciton-polariton condensates, part light and part matter. Dirac cones in such lattices normally come in pairs, and breaking symmetries opens both to create a topological gap. Here, breaking inversion symmetry by splitting one sublattice's pillars, plus time-reversal breaking from a magnetic field and spin-orbit coupling, leaves the cones unpaired in the spectrum of the device.

Even without a full spectral gap, one-way edge states still emerge and can turn corners of the array. Resonant pumping brings bistability, letting operators excite chosen edge states selectively with light. The team obtains a stable, localised edge soliton that circulates around the rim of the structure indefinitely without radiating away. The platform points to new devices for nonlinear topological photonics in practice.
arxiv-2606-17507:
Xu and colleagues present a 2026 arXiv paper on using language models to mark student answers for high-stakes exam preparation, with the marking grounded in official curriculum documents. Prompt tricks alone are not enough at that level of stakes, the authors argue. Their pipeline, built with an industry partner, first pins down a question's topics, subtopics, and cognitive demand, then assembles official context from syllabus artefacts and marking guidelines issued by education authorities.

Syllabus intent enters through concrete items: prescribed verbs, stated outcomes, performance band descriptors, glossary definitions, and marking principles. A staged workflow drafts question-specific rubrics, then derives the marking criteria used to score each response. Early evaluation shows marking close to human tutors, with justifications that trace more clearly to official sources. The pipeline already runs inside an online study platform, where override data are being collected.
arxiv-2606-17707:
Yang and colleagues present a 2026 arXiv paper asking whether generative recommenders trap users in information cocoons more or less than the classic kind. Recommenders feed on their own past suggestions, narrowing what users see until tastes harden into bubbles. Generative systems differ fundamentally: they emit items as code sequences rather than scoring fixed catalogue entries, which might change how cocoons form. The team built RecLoop, a closed-loop simulation where language-model user agents interact with recommenders over many feedback cycles with periodic retraining switched on.

Thousands of agents shopped two product data sets across fifteen cycles in the simulation. Generative recommenders preserved broader exposure and slowed the drift toward sameness across users compared with sequential baselines. Yet concentration still grew inside the generated code space itself, a model-level cocoon the authors measure separately. Token choice and model scale strongly shaped how severe the effect became.
arxiv-2606-17807:
Olleik and colleagues study how Lebanese households cope when the public electricity grid fails for long stretches. Lebanon has near-universal electrification on paper, yet chronic shortages shape daily energy use. Drawing on an original survey of one thousand households, the 2026 paper examines both backup supply choices and changes in how people use power.

Households rely mainly on diesel generators, solar panels paired with batteries, or hybrid mixes of the two. Wealth strongly shapes who can afford backup and how much of their demand gets met, and a shift toward solar and batteries is clear among better-off families. The authors also document wasted solar output, load shifting, and suppressed demand, arguing that backup access and unmet demand must be distinguished in energy policy.
arxiv-2606-18607:
Ni and Lai propose a method for finding unknown energy potentials inside phase field models from observed data, in a 2026 paper on inverse problems for materials modeling. Phase field simulations track how microstructures evolve using equations such as Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard, but the nonlinear potentials driving them are hard to measure, which limits how predictive the models can be.

Their Dual Time Phase Field Inversion framework turns recovery into a fitting problem matching model output to the measured final field. They prove the measured field is differentiable in the unknown potential and that the regularized objective is locally convex, so a local optimum exists. Automatic differentiation supplies the gradients cheaply. In tests the method accurately rebuilt both polynomial and logarithmic potentials and stayed robust under measurement noise. It extends to field-dependent mobility and joint parameter identification in coupled systems.
arxiv-2606-18807:
Belova, Dementiev, and Sagunov ask whether machine-learned predictions can speed up the exact exponential-time algorithms used for NP-hard problems, in a 2026 theoretical computer science paper. Learning-augmented algorithms had shown them beating worst-case guarantees for polynomial-time problems. But exact algorithms for problems such as feedback vertex set, hitting set, and weighted satisfiability live under exponential running times and conjectured barriers.

The authors answer yes, with a general approach that adds to a family of exact algorithms for subset selection problems. A noisy predictor only just better than random guessing already suffices to provably shrink the search space. The runtime speedup scales smoothly with prediction quality. That is an information leverage effect, in which a linear amount of signal tames an exponential search. The assumptions are weak: pairwise independence of prediction errors suffices. One variant does not need to know the predictor's accuracy.
arxiv-2606-19207:
Xie studies extrema of Gaussian fields with a microscopic slowdown in a 2026 probability paper. The family of fields has a covariance structure that slows down unevenly at small scales. A tuning parameter moves the field between a log profile at one end and a log-log profile at the other. In one dimension the objects act like branching Brownian motion in a cooling environment.

The correct centering of the maximum at large times is found. It then proves tightness of the recentered maximum. The leading growth of the maximum varies linearly with the tuning parameter. The second-order correction behaves differently. It shows a phase transition at a threshold value of the parameter, where the correction changes form. Extrema of log-correlated fields link to branching processes and to multiplicative chaos, so sharp centering results feed several active areas of probability at once.
arxiv-2606-19507:
Meredith Shea studies a split Aztec diamond tiling model in 2026. An Aztec diamond is a diamond-shaped region tiled by dominoes, a classic model in statistical mechanics. Shea splits the region into two unequal parts whose sizes stay fixed in ratio as the diamond grows.

Each part carries its own two-periodic weighting, a repeating pattern of tile weights. The larger part is the dominant side, the smaller the non-dominant side, and their border is the interface. Shea derives an integral formula for the model's correlation kernel. From it comes a partial account of the scaling limit, plus a conjecture for the rest. The dominant side's limit shape matches the standard two-periodic diamond and ignores the other side. The smaller side's shape is new, depending on both weightings and the interface position. A full limit shape follows when the dominant weighting parameter tends to zero.
arxiv-2606-19707:
Douglas Bridges builds an axiomatic theory of justification inside constructive set theory in 2026. Constructive Morse Set Theory treats every term as also a formula, and vice versa. That feature suits a formal account of what it means for one statement to justify another.

Bridges introduces a new notion, written jst P p, for the claim that P proves or justifies p. The reading follows the BHK interpretation of intuitionistic logic, where proofs are constructions. Axioms for the notion come first, stated inside set theory itself. Many consequences then follow by derivation. Under stated restrictions, the axioms align with the intended BHK readings of the intuitionistic logic axioms. Justification logic usually lives in modal systems apart from set theory. Bridges instead grounds proof talk in the same universe as the mathematics it describes.
arxiv-2606-19907:
Jan Kelleter and six colleagues fight seismic gravity noise at the future Einstein Telescope with neural networks in 2026. Seismic waves tug test masses through their own gravity, a Newtonian noise floor for low-frequency listening. Seismometer arrays can predict that noise so it can be subtracted.

A simulation breeds density fluctuations from random plane waves and Gaussian wave packets. It computes both the ground displacement field and the resulting Newtonian noise. Neural networks and the classic Wiener filter compete at prediction. On near-stationary wave fields the two approaches tie, with networks slightly ahead. Single dominating events, long or short, change the picture sharply. Convolutional and graph networks beat the Wiener filter by factors of fifteen to eighty there. Noise amplitude spectra fall by factors of ten to thirty in those event cases.
arxiv-2606-20207:
Ruilin Hu and five colleagues prove that the 3D Navier-Stokes equations for fluids of varying density have strong solutions. The solutions start from unusually rough initial data. Their 2026 paper studies the inhomogeneous incompressible system, where density is transported by the flow. The velocity must start in a space called VMO-inverse, rougher than the classical energy class, and the density is smooth with a positive lower bound.

Local existence of strong solutions is established for such data. If the density is slightly smoother and the initial perturbation and velocity are small in the right norms, the solution exists globally. The proof uses transport estimates for density regularity and a new freezing coefficient method for the momentum equation. Knowing exactly which starting roughness still yields a well-behaved solution defines the theory's reach.
arxiv-2606-20307:
Huai-Dong Cao, Xiaofeng Sun, and Yingying Zhang give a dynamical construction of Hermitian-Einstein metrics on stable holomorphic vector bundles. Their 2026 paper builds on recent results for the prescribed Hermitian-Yang-Mills tensor and its twisted variants. A Hermitian-Einstein metric is a canonical geometry for a bundle: its curvature, contracted against the Kähler form, is a constant multiple of the identity. Stability, a slope condition on subsheaves, is the property expected to guarantee such a metric exists.

The authors' iteration produces the metric dynamically, and the construction extends to Higgs bundles. In an appendix, the heat flow method yields a new proof that solutions of the twisted tensor equation exist and are unique, plus its Higgs generalization. The results sit inside the Donaldson-Uhlenbeck-Yau circle linking stability to canonical metrics. A dynamical route matters because it suggests algorithms, not just existence theorems.
arxiv-2606-20707:
Christian Internò and many colleagues introduce GeoPhys in 2026, a fast way to judge whether a video event is physically plausible. Humans spot impossible events in milliseconds. Machine methods are often slow and costly. They may rely on large multimodal judges or special training changes. GeoPhys argues that plausibility signals already sit in the frame embeddings of frozen image encoders, as five geometric properties.

Those signals correlate with human brain responses to object permanence violations. GeoPhys also separates implausible from realistic videos with high scores: 98.3 percent on LikePhys and 93.3 percent on IntPhys2. Several large video models perform near chance on the same tests. Used as a verifier during generation, GeoPhys lifts one large video model from 50.01 to 64.50 percent on PhysicsIQ, at lower cost. A cheap geometry check could help filter unrealistic generated video before costly human review.
arxiv-2606-21007:
Hajar Aziz and ten colleagues investigate a distant galaxy nicknamed lil gal in 2026, found by chance in Webb telescope images of a nearby galaxy. In two mid-infrared bands it looks like a spiral galaxy with a central bulge. In a third band, a second peak appears offset from the bulge. That raises three candidate explanations: a clumpy disk, an unrelated background galaxy, or a merger.

Multi-band analysis across Webb and Hubble images gives a photometric redshift near one. Spectroscopy from Keck reveals two sets of emission lines. They correspond to the two sources, at nearly the same redshift. The pair is therefore a merging galaxy system. Projected separation is about five kiloparsecs. A serendipitous find becomes a case study of galaxy assembly at cosmic noon, when mergers helped build the galaxies seen today.
arxiv-2606-21107:
Minwoo Kim, Junyong Park, and Sungkyu Jung propose an empirical Bayes method in 2026 to improve the utility of differentially private statistics without weakening privacy. Differential privacy protects individuals by adding noise. The Gaussian mechanism is simple and widely used. Its output is noisy by design, and many enhanced methods are complex or costly. Their idea is to denoise the output after the fact.

Empirical Bayes estimation takes the Gaussian mechanism output as its only input. It shrinks noise using structure learned from the output itself. Mean-squared error falls while the privacy level stays the same. Numerical studies cover histogram release, principal component analysis, and linear regression. The approach often beats existing private algorithms. A simple post-step that helps many tasks at once is valuable, because privacy budgets are precious and complex private pipelines are hard to deploy correctly.
arxiv-2606-21307:
Jiacheng Wang and seven colleagues propose TASER in 2026, a continual learning framework for models that must absorb very different tasks in sequence, from math reasoning to legal summaries. Most continual learning assumes tasks resemble each other, so fixed capacity either forgets old skills or wastes room. TASER instead grows a library of small atomic skills, deciding for each new task how many fresh skills to add, based on task divergence and model uncertainty.

Orthogonality checks keep the skills distinct and reusable, and a light gating mechanism routes each task to the skills it needs. The team also releases HeteroCLBench, nineteen tasks across nine cognitive dimensions under one sequential protocol. On that benchmark TASER beats strong baselines, learning new tasks while forgetting less, a step toward models that keep pace with shifting real workloads.
arxiv-2606-21607:
Di Yang and four colleagues present T-MOR in 2026, a framework that learns human action representations from skeleton data while borrowing supervision from video and language. Vision-language models read appearance well but barely model motion, even though actions are defined by how bodies move over time. T-MOR aligns skeleton sequences with matching video and text through multi-modal contrastive learning, then runs at test time on lightweight skeleton input alone.

Training uses PoseCap-1M, a new dataset of over one million synchronized video, skeleton, and text triplets spanning diverse activities. Across benchmarks including Toyota Smarthome, UAV-Human, Penn Action, and Charades, T-MOR improves action classification and frame-wise detection over prior methods. It also generalizes strongly in few-shot and zero-shot tests, evidence that motion-centered representations transfer well between tasks.
arxiv-2606-21707:
Favaro and Fortini work on a classic statistics problem in 2026: estimating sums that mix observed values with hidden ones. Empirical Bayes methods handle such sums under mixture models, but older versions lean on narrow assumptions or cover only a few target functions. Their paper develops a more flexible alternative called quasi-Bayes empirical Bayes, designed to stay broad and cheap to compute.

The method builds the mixing distribution step by step using Newton's algorithm, then plugs that estimate into the target sum. Error bars come from large-sample theory, which describes the estimate's long-run spread with a Gaussian limit law. The authors prove the quasi-Bayes and true Bayes estimates merge as samples grow, and that the method stays consistent when the model is right. Tests on synthetic and real data matched or beat older empirical Bayes methods in accuracy and stability.
arxiv-2606-21907:
Vashistha, Sarkar, and Farahi tackle deconvolution in 2026, the problem of recovering a hidden signal's distribution after measurement noise has blurred it. Instruments rarely record the quantity itself, and for flexible generative models the formula needed by classic methods is often impossible to write down. Their answer is a likelihood-free method built on simulation based inference.

The method fits a latent generative model so its noise-blurred distribution matches the observed data distribution, using a convolutional maximum mean discrepancy loss as the yardstick. The learned density then acts as an empirical prior for denoising single measurements. The framework handles noise of varying size across observations and works with rich model families such as Gaussian mixtures and normalizing flows. The authors prove finite-sample error bounds and convergence rates that match classical theory: polynomial rates for ordinary-smooth noise and logarithmic rates for super-smooth noise.
arxiv-2606-22007:
Price reviews, in 2026, the state of Monte Carlo event generators for future lepton colliders, software that simulates particle collisions event by event so theory can be compared with detector data. Future lepton collider programmes will demand far more from these tools than current machines do. The review, an invited workshop contribution, selects the challenges Price judges most pressing rather than attempting complete coverage.

The topics include electroweak corrections, beam radiation, and beam dynamics, all of which distort the clean collisions lepton machines are famous for. Quantum chromodynamics calculations and the modelling of how quarks settle into ordinary particles also need sharper treatment. Price frames these tools as the link between theory and measurement: without fully exclusive simulated events, the goals cannot be checked against reality. The discussion aims to guide where effort should concentrate before the new colliders arrive.
arxiv-2606-22107:
Oke and Dossa build, in 2026, a rigorous framework for supersymmetric quantum systems whose momentum operator is deformed by geometry. Earlier work ensured it behaved correctly only through boundary conditions. Their construction makes it strictly self-adjoint by design, for both linear and quadratic deformation shapes, inside one scheme.

The scheme yields exact energy spectra and reveals a hidden su(1,1) symmetry in the systems. The authors also give the first full heat treatment, computing the partition function by the Euler-Maclaurin method. Deformation reshapes the density of states in distinct ways. The linear shape produces a divergent peak in heat capacity, from states piling up near a top energy. The quadratic shape instead saturates the heat capacity below the Dulong-Petit limit.
arxiv-2606-22207:
Vera introduces Lexical Consensus in 2026, a test framework for studying whether software agents can learn grounded word meanings from experience. Agents see frozen DINOv2 visual features and must acquire Carroll-style invented words for visual concepts. A family of simple learners, from centroid prototypes to exemplar nearest neighbours, is tested across controlled settings.

The central finding is a robust perceptual-coherence gradient. Native categories are learned most easily, coherent overreach remains learnable, disjunctive concepts degrade, and far-disjunctive ones approach chance. A pre-registered experiment over CIFAR-100 confirms perceptual distance, not semantic closeness, governs the gradient: the perceptual predictor explains a substantial share of variance while the semantic one adds almost none. Exemplar models beat centroid prototypes at label-to-image retrieval for multi-peaked concepts. Frozen perceptual geometry thus both enables grounding and bounds what can be learned.
arxiv-2606-22307:
Dang and colleagues propose Manifold Restore Mixing in 2026, a data augmentation method for protein representation learning that repairs the structural damage such methods usually cause. Standard methods add useful variation but risk disrupting protein structure and function. Homology modelling tools preserve structure but reduce diversity. The authors first document these structure defects and the performance loss they cause in existing methods.

Their method mixes the hidden states of original and augmented protein data, inspired by manifold mixup. The mixed samples restore structural information lost in augmentation while keeping diverse variation. A sample difficulty scheduler adjusts the mixup spread during training, feeding the model ever harder mixed samples. Experiments across several backbones and downstream tasks show the method works well and transfers. Code and weights are released openly.
arxiv-2606-22507:
Yoshihito Kuno and Takahiro Orito study what noise does to a topological quantum state in this 2026 physics paper. Their starting point is an extended cluster state, a symmetry protected topological phase guarded by many subsystem symmetries. Decoherence, the leakage of quantum information into the environment, is usually treated as purely destructive.

Applying decoherence to one subsystem at a time induces local charge fluctuations there, while the untouched subsystems settle into a mixed symmetry protected state. Step by step, a hierarchy of such mixed-state phases emerges, each still guarded by the surviving strong symmetries. The phases can be told apart by Rényi-2 string order parameters. The hierarchy ends when the last subsystem falls into a strong-to-weak symmetry breaking state with glassy GHZ-type long-range entanglement. The work shows decoherence can organize a whole family of nontrivial mixed states, not just destroy order.
arxiv-2606-22607:
Alexandru Enciu and eleven colleagues report detector electronics for a nuclear physics experiment in this 2026 paper. The HYDRA time projection chamber is a dedicated pion tracker built to study hypernuclei, exotic nuclei containing a strange quark, within the R3B experiment at GSI/FAIR in Germany. Its readout uses the VMM3a chip inside the Scalable Readout System, offering high rates with precise charge and timing measurement.

The team adapted that readout architecture to the chamber's pad plane. The work covers custom adapter boards, power distribution, and synchronization with the wider R3B data acquisition system. A series of laboratory and integration tests then evaluated the full readout chain. Results demonstrate reliable operation and precise timing performance. The chain proved compatible with the R3B acquisition framework, establishing the system as a suitable readout solution for the chamber. The paper is an instrumentation report rather than a physics result.
arxiv-2606-22707:
Peter Renkel offers a test of a quantum collapse theory in this 2026 paper. Continuous Spontaneous Localization says quantum superpositions collapse on their own at a rate growing with mass, an idea needing sensitive experiments to confirm or exclude. His design uses a trapped nanoparticle as a reversible pointer, rather than preparing the particle itself in superposition.

A microscopic two-branch system applies opposite weak forces, briefly amplifying which-branch information into separated pointer positions. After one trap period the positions and momenta recombine. Ordinary quantum mechanics then predicts the microscopic coherence is recovered. The collapse theory instead predicts an irreversible visibility loss accumulated while the pointer's mass was separated. For a nanoparticle of 10^-18 kilograms driven by a force of 10^-21 newtons at 0.4 kelvin, the sensitivity reaches collapse rates near 10^-11 per second in the aggressive setup. Xun Chen and colleagues probe a frustrated magnet called GdZnPO in a 2026 condensed matter paper. In frustrated magnets, competing interactions stop spins from settling into a simple pattern. The result can be a spin liquid, a state with restless spins and no fixed order. GdZnPO arranges its large spins on a honeycomb lattice. Theory had suggested its many spiral states could cooperate into a spiral spin liquid. The team tests that idea with nuclear magnetic resonance, which reads local magnetism through atomic nuclei.

Chen and colleagues find uniform magnetization and lively low-energy spin motion at middle field strengths, persisting to very low temperature with no sign of broken symmetry. That behavior supports a spin liquid state. At weaker fields, a faint stripe order appears at low temperature, yet strong fluctuations remain. The spin size only weakly lifts the spiral degeneracy, leaving order subtle and dynamics robust.
arxiv-2606-23307:
Chang Han and colleagues propose a new route to primordial black holes in a 2026 cosmology paper. Primordial black holes form when huge early density ripples collapse. Making enough of them needs a strong boost to curvature ripples on small scales. The authors place that boost after inflation, during a stiff epoch when the universe's expansion behaves unusually. Primordial magnetic fields carry an electromagnetic stress with a vector part. That vector part sources metric vector ripples, which stay nearly constant through the stiff epoch and persistently feed second-order scalar ripples.

Han and colleagues show the induced curvature ripples grow toward the low-frequency edge of the stiff band with a steep characteristic slope. For magnetic fields from a standard Ratra-type generation scenario, the ripples can produce black holes in abundance. The yield could make up a substantial fraction of the dark matter.
arxiv-2606-23507:

The second quantum revolution advances computing, communication, and sensing together. Education has raced ahead on computing while sensing stays largely overlooked. To find entry points, the authors analyze six widely used textbooks spanning modern physics, quantum mechanics, and quantum computing. They tag every excerpt mentioning sensing-related keywords and record the context of each appearance. Network maps then show which keywords appear in which contexts, and how often.

Pradeep and Zwickl score the tagged excerpts with a rubric for conceptual and mathematical depth. Coverage varies widely across subjects in both content and depth. Spin-first and position-first textbooks differ notably in how they treat core concepts like superposition and entanglement. The authors also mine a database of over eight thousand quantum course descriptions for sensing mentions.
arxiv-2606-23607:
Li and Shen scale up a method for merging separately trained neural networks into one, in a 2026 paper on deep learning. Linear mode connectivity means two models can be joined by a straight line in weight space without the loss spiking midway. When that holds, merging is as simple as averaging weights. In practice, trained models sit in mismatched arrangements, since many weight patterns compute the same function, and naive averaging hits a loss barrier.

Their framework applies function preserving transformations to align the two models. A dual learning procedure then trains both transformations at once, each moving toward a shared straight path. On WikiText tasks the method reaches near zero loss barriers at medium scale. A large vision transformer keeps accuracy above sixty nine percent along the path, and billion parameter models show only small barriers.

Electroencephalography uses electrodes on the scalp to record brain activity. Real recordings lose channels randomly to bad contacts and device differences, and high density setups are costly and cumbersome. Spatial super resolution aims to recover the full signal set from sparse measurements, but most methods learn one fixed mapping between set layouts and break when the missing pattern changes.

The authors recast the task as learning a shared scalp field from whichever channels are observed. An encoder compresses the available channels, together with their coordinates, into one latent condition. A decoder then answers queries at any electrode coordinate, even locations never seen in training. On several datasets the method cuts error sharply for unseen electrodes.

avicenna-liber-canonis-1507:
Avicenna's Canon of Medicine appears here in a Latin printing made at Venice in 1507. Gerard of Cremona had translated the huge Arabic work into Latin in the twelfth century. Avicenna, a Persian physician and philosopher, wrote the Canon in the early 1000s, and it grew into the most used medical book in the world.

The Canon gathers Greek, Indian, and Persian healing into one ordered system of theory, drugs, and treatment. It runs to about a million words across five books, covering fevers, organs, and compound medicines. European universities taught medicine from this text for some five hundred years. The 1507 Venice edition shows the book in its Renaissance form, still the doctor's bible long after its author's death.
bakunin-oeuvres-vol1-1907:
James Guillaume edited the French collected works of Mikhail Bakunin, and the first volume appeared in 1907. Bakunin, the Russian revolutionary who died in 1876, was anarchism's founding thinker. His papers had been scattered across Europe, and Guillaume, an old comrade, spent years gathering them into print.

Volume 1 collects Bakunin's early writings, including his break with Marx and his plans for a federal, stateless order. The texts argue that freedom cannot be granted by any state and must grow from free communes linked by choice. Guillaume added notes that place each piece in Bakunin's restless life. The six volumes that followed made this edition the main source for studying anarchism at its source.
bibliotheca-chemico-curiosa-d-mangeti-en: Bibliotheca chemico-curiosa, 1707. The curious chemical library. This book preserves that collection. Those who study the era will use it. The archive keeps the paper open to all. Its pages add to the record of the past.
blackwood-willows-1907:
Two friends canoe down the Danube in Algernon Blackwood's short novel The Willows, first told in 1907. They camp on a small isle of sand and willow trees. Wind, water, and odd sounds wear at their nerves night by night.

No beast steps into view. Dread comes from a sense that vast, cold powers press close to our world. H. P. Lovecraft ranked the tale at the top of weird prose. It still sets the bar for tales of fear in wild places. The two men row, camp, and doubt their own senses as signs mount. Blackwood lets sound and wind do the work that beasts do in lesser tales.
brentano-untersuchungen-zur-sinnespsycho:
Brentano's Investigations in the Psychology of the Senses appeared in German in 1907. Brentano had founded a new, careful study of mental life in Vienna, training students who spread his methods widely. Late in his career he turned to a basic question: how do seeing, hearing, and touch give us the world?

The studies take each sense apart, asking what a sensation contains and how the mind builds objects from it. Brentano argues against loose talk about the senses and demands exact description of what is actually given. His method, describing experience before explaining it, became a mark of his school. The book shows philosophy's keenest eye at work in the inner workshop of perception, where psychology and philosophy had not yet fully parted.
brocquiere-travels-johnes-1807:
Bertrandon de La Brocquiere rode east in 1432, part pilgrim and part spy for Burgundy. Thomas Johnes's 1807 English version tells his trek through Ottoman lands and home again, much of it in disguise. His eye for armies, customs, and roads never rests.

Brocquiere notes what Turks eat, wear, and ride, and how their camps are run. His report gave Europe an early, detailed picture of the Turks. Pilgrim's piety and spy's cunning share every page. The account stands as travel writing with a secret brief, five centuries old and still fresh in its curiosity and nerve.
carrington-physical-phenomena-spirituali:
Hereward Carrington wrote The Physical Phenomena of Spiritualism in 1907 as a field manual of mediumship. Carrington had investigated the medium Eusapia Palladino at first hand. His book sorts the famous physical phenomena into the fraudulent and the genuine. Table turns, materializations, and spirit hands all face his tests.

He gives a full account of the methods used to fake such wonders. Readers learn the tricks of slate writing, cabinet work, and tied mediums. His criticism weighs what little evidence survives such checks. The first edition became a handbook for investigators on both sides. It stays useful as a guide to period stagecraft. Skeptics and believers both cite it.
catherine-siena-dialogue-thorold-1907:
Catherine of Siena told her Dialogue to scribes as she prayed, it is said. Algar Thorold gave the work English dress in 1907. Catherine was a young nun of Siena who swayed popes and towns. She died at the age of three and thirty in 1380.

God speaks with the soul on how He guides the world and each life. The bridge of Christ, with its steps, frames much of the talk. Calls to mend the Church ring through the last parts. The book is one of the great talks with God of the mid ages.
chapman-bussy-dambois-1607:
George Chapman wrote Bussy D'Ambois, first staged around 1604, and its sequel The Revenge of Bussy D'Ambois some years later. F. Boas edited the two plays together in the edition here. Chapman, the translator of Homer, brought a poet's weight to the stage.

Bussy, a bold French courtier, rises by daring and falls by love and intrigue at the court of Henri III. The sequel follows his brother Clermont, a Stoic answer to Bussy's fire. Chapman's verse is dense, learned, and thunderous, prized by readers who like their tragedy heroic. The pair shows the Elizabethan superman at his rise and in his ruins.
cia-0000008007:
Political development in South Vietnam posed hard problems, and a November 1966 CIA study took them up directly. Saigon's generals had cycled through governments while the war against the Viet Cong and North Vietnam widened. Buddhist protests and regional loyalties strained the state further.

The study asks whether South Vietnam could build stable politics within about a year. That question mattered because military aid alone could not create legitimacy. Readers get an insider view of doubts that public statements often hid. The paper shows analysts grading an ally's weaknesses frankly, in the middle of a war America was escalating.
cia-0000009807:
A Viet Cong prison camp for American and South Vietnamese prisoners is located in a July 1971 item, in a place the title cuts off. Joint camps were common in the south, where the Viet Cong held their captives near the fighting. The item's job is the location itself.

A bare location still carried weight: it told searchers where to look and airmen where danger sat. It also let later sightings from the same area lock onto a known site. Many entries in the prison map began as one-line fixes like this. The file preserves the fix as filed, before description or confirmation could be added.

Rumor said an American pilot was seen being carried through a village near a Laotian place the title cuts off at Ban, a November 1966 item records. The heading itself calls the report rumor, the weakest grade in the files. A carried pilot was likely wounded, which sharpened the claim's pull.

Rumor reports were kept because some rumors, checked, became facts. Others dissolved, and the file would show that too in time. Analysts had to hold both outcomes open at once. This entry preserves the holding pattern: a wounded man, a village, and a story not yet believed or dismissed.

Meeting number nineteen falls on July 20, 1961, inside the Yoga summer phase of the debriefings. The numbering's gaps hint at sessions unrecorded, lost, or filed elsewhere in the case. Summer's work was underway in earnest by then, day after day. The colonel was answering for his Moscow weeks. His handlers measured what he brought against what they had asked him to find.

The nineteenth session's record carries the phase forward in order. Behind the numbers sits a rhythm of travel, risk, and talk. For readers, the gaps in the sequence testify silently to all the file cannot show.
cia-0000013207:
Raw reporting from the ground fills a field information report from October 1970. Its subject is an American prisoner of war in Tuyen Due province. Field reports reached Langley unpolished, straight from the source's mouth. A case officer's pen passed them on with little editing. That roughness was precisely their value. The report preserves what was known about one captive's place and condition. Such fragments fed the great accounting of the missing men. For readers, it is the war's facts at their freshest, before summaries replaced them.
cia-0000015307: A letter to Leon Davidson from J. S. Harman fills a CIA file dated March 5, 1958. Harman thanks Davidson for his letter of March 1. cia-0000042907:

He also had to face an army that held the suspects in its ranks. The file shows a civilian president planning his way through a case in which every step risked a break with the men who held the guns.
cia-0000045207:

Inside, the two camps' readings of the crisis sit in one file. The contrast between them is the country's split in miniature. One side blamed the government for the crime itself. The other blamed the same government for softness toward the criminals who had seized the president's daughter. The record holds both voices on the same page, which lets readers measure the distance between El Salvador's extremes in their own words.

Chile's copper, its strong parties, and its open politics made it a country analysts followed closely. The forecast weighs the government's prospects and the pressures around it. Written twenty years before the 1973 coup, it cannot foresee that ending. It does show the questions the agency was already asking about Chilean democracy: how firm it was, and what might shake it.

The document weighs that timing question directly. Its title alone sums up the invasion debate in a single sentence. For readers, it shows the agency pausing to question its own course before the die was cast. Few entries in the file state their doubt so plainly on the record. The question would be answered by events that spring, at heavy cost to the invasion force.
