The sample shows the act's contents. Title I covers conservation and management of fisheries. Its parts take up combined harm to fish stocks and the reach of the Caribbean Council. They cover regional councils and what fishery plans must hold. They also cover limited access rights, checks on nature, and crisis rules. Joint enforcement deals and a shift to lasting fisheries close the title in view.
plaw-109-480-2007:
Democracy aid for Belarus is renewed by Public Law 109-480, the Belarus Democracy Reauthorization Act of 2006. It was signed on January 12, 2007. It reauthorizes the Belarus Democracy Act of 2004.

The act rewrites the findings of the 2004 law. Congress found a pattern of clear, uncorrected breaches of human rights by the Belarus government. It found flawed presidential and assembly elections that undercut trust in the state's rule. The March 19, 2006, presidential vote failed world pledges for free elections, the findings say. They charge the regime of Aleksandr Lukashenka with seizing power by an illegal vote. That vote, they say, scrapped the elected parliament and lifted term limits.
plaw-109-481-2007:
Misuse of aid emblems is barred by Public Law 109-481, the Geneva Distinctive Emblems Protection Act of 2006. It was signed on January 12, 2007. It amends title 18 to guard the Red Crescent and the Third Protocol emblem, the Red Crystal.

The act adds section 706a to the code. Wearing or showing either emblem to fake a link to an aid society is a crime. So is plain use of the emblems or their names by those with no right to them. The penalty is a fine, up to six months in prison, or both. Groups with a right under the Geneva Conventions of 1949 may still use them. Those groups include national societies and the International Committee of the Red Cross.
plaw-109-482-2007:
The national health research giant is reshaped by Public Law 109-482, the National Institutes of Health Reform Act of 2006. It was signed on January 15, 2007. It revises and extends the powers of the institutes under title IV of the health act.

Title I is called NIH Reform. Its first part restates how the institutes are organized. The National Institutes of Health is an agency of the Public Health Service. The part then lists its research institutes and centers. They include the National Cancer Institute and the institutes for heart, lung, and blood health. They also include those for aging, allergy, child health, eye health, and nerve disorders. The sample stops partway through that list.

In building the program, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs is to weigh the special needs of those veterans. The needs of older veterans, at high risk for depression and suicide, count as well. The program is set by a new section 1720F. Its parts begin with required training for staff. The sample ends inside that training clause.
plaw-110-111-2007:
Yearly cost-of-living raises for veterans come in Public Law 110-111, the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2007. It lifts pay for veterans hurt in service and support pay for kin of some who died.

They cover the clothing allowance and support pay for spouses and children left behind. Each sum rises by the same rate as Social Security benefits for that date. The sample ends inside that rate clause.
plaw-110-112-2007:
A Georgia veterans hospital takes a lawmaker's name in Public Law 110-112 of 2007. The Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Augusta is named the Charlie Norwood Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center.

The sample shows the act's findings in full. Norwood served in the Army Dental Corps in Vietnam in 1968, earning the Combat Medical Badge and two Bronze Stars. He gave dental, emergency, and surgical care to troops, Vietnamese civilians, and prisoners of war. He later gave 25 years of private dental care in the Augusta area. In the House from 1995, he pushed for stronger military and veterans health care, the findings say.
plaw-110-113-2007:
Court reach in September 11 cases is widened by Public Law 110-113, the Procedural Fairness for September 11 Victims Act of 2007. It grants nationwide subpoena power for suits under the September 11 Victim Compensation Fund of 2001.

Congress found that the fund gives one federal claim, heard in the Southern District of New York. It covers harm from the four hijacked flights of September 11, 2001. Court rules, though, bound subpoena service to the district or 100 miles from it, save where a law says more. Many witnesses in such cases live far from New York. The act answers by letting trial subpoenas be served at any place in the nation.
plaw-110-114-2007:
Water projects across the country are cleared by Public Law 110-114, the Water Resources Development Act of 2007. It backs saving and growth of water and linked resources. It lets the Secretary of the Army build projects to improve rivers and harbors.

The sample shows the act's contents. Title I lists project approvals and small projects of many kinds. They span flood harm cuts, bank guards in crises, and shipping works. They also span green gains, shore guards, and clearing of snags and silt. Title II sets general terms, such as non-federal cost shares and funds to speed permits. It also covers dredged material disposal and far harbors.
plaw-110-115-2007:
A Florida museum wins a national title in Public Law 110-115 of 2007. The Navy UDT-SEAL Museum in Fort Pierce is named the official national museum of Navy SEALs and those who came before them.

Congress found that the SEALs trace their roots to the Navy Frogmen of World War II. Fort Pierce is known as the birthplace of the Frogmen, where thousands trained in demolition units. The museum is the sole one given to the story of the SEALs and their forerunners alone. A nonprofit group of current and former SEALs runs its funds, work, and holdings. It opened in 1985 and holds objects and photos that tell that history.
plaw-110-116-2007:
Defense funds for a new year are granted by Public Law 110-116 of 2007. It makes appropriations for the Department of Defense for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2008.

They also cover research and testing, revolving funds, and other defense programs. Related agencies and general terms close the division. Division B holds further continuing appropriations for 2008. The sample shows the act's contents and the start of Division A, then ends.

plaw-110-132-2007:
Funds to save elephants, rhinos, and tigers are renewed by Public Law 110-132 of 2007. Its title is the Multinational Species Conservation Funds Reauthorization Act of 2007. It reauthorizes two older acts on those animals.

The acts are the African Elephant Conservation Act and the Rhinoceros and Tiger Conservation Act of 1994. For each act, the same three changes are made. Notice of a cleared project no longer goes to each country where work is planned. The cap on office costs rises from 80,000 dollars to 100,000 dollars. Funds are cleared for the years 2007 through 2012. The act was signed on December 6, 2007.
plaw-110-133-2007: Asian elephants gain renewed aid under Public Law 110-133, the Asian Elephant Conservation Reauthorization Act of 2007. It reauthorizes the Asian Elephant Conservation Act of 1997. Three changes are made. Notice of a cleared project goes to the Administrator alone, not to each country as well. The cap on office costs rises from 80,000 dollars to 100,000 dollars. Funds are cleared for the years 2007 through 2012. The act was signed on December 6, 2007.
plaw-110-134-2007:
Head Start is renewed and reshaped by Public Law 110-134, the Improving Head Start for School Readiness Act of 2007. It reauthorizes the Head Start Act to improve quality and widen access for young children.

The sample shows the act's contents, a list of 29 parts. Early parts cover aid sums, how funds are shared out, and which groups may run programs. Standards and checks on programs follow. Later parts cover the move from Head Start into school and joint work with K-12 schools. They cover staff training, studies, wage fairness, and parent consent for health services. plaw-110-135-2007:
Older airline pilots gain years in the cockpit under Public Law 110-135, the Fair Treatment for Experienced Pilots Act of 2007. It amends title 49 to change age standards for pilots in commercial flying.

A new section 44729 lets a pilot serve in multi-crew work until age 65. The work covered is that under part 121 of the flight rules. For flights abroad, a pilot over 60 may lead the crew only if a second pilot in the cockpit is under 60. That limit ends when world rules change to match. The old age 60 retirement rule ends at once, on the day the act passed.
plaw-110-136-2007: Small business programs gain a short added span under Public Law 110-136 of 2007. It amends the act that last extended Small Business Administration powers. Each date in that act moves from December 15, 2007, to May 23, 2008. That extends programs under the Small Business Act and the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to the new date. The change takes effect on December 15, 2007.
plaw-110-137-2007: Stopgap federal funding is stretched by one week in Public Law 110-137, a joint resolution of 2007. It further amends Public Law 110-92, the continuing appropriations act for fiscal year 2008. The date in section 106(3) of that act is struck and December 21, 2007, is put in. The resolution passed both chambers on December 13 and was signed on December 14, 2007.
plaw-110-138-2007:
Trade with Peru is put into force by Public Law 110-138, the United States-Peru Trade Promotion Agreement Implementation Act of 2007. It carries out the trade pact named in its title.

The sample shows the act's contents. Title I approves the pact and sets how it takes force, as with the Central America pact in an earlier law in this set. It covers the pact's tie to state law and dispute panels. Title II covers customs work: tariff changes and added duties on some farm goods. It also covers rules of origin, user fees, and false origin claims. Record keeping and checks on textile and clothing trade close the list in view.
plaw-110-139-2007: A name full of meaning is given to a Capitol hall by Public Law 110-139 of 2007. The great hall of the Capitol Visitor Center is to be known as Emancipation Hall. Any mention of the great hall in a law, rule, or regulation is to be read as a mention of Emancipation Hall. The act took effect on the day it was signed, December 18, 2007.
plaw-110-14-2007: Santa Fe names its courthouse in Public Law 110-14 of 2007. The courthouse at South Federal Place is named the Santiago E. Campos United States Courthouse. Any mention of the courthouse in a federal law, map, rule, paper, or record is to use that name. The bill passed the House on March 6, 2007, and the Senate on March 9, and was signed on March 21.
plaw-110-140-2007:
Energy freedom and safety are the broad aims of Public Law 110-140, the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007. Its heading lists those aims in full.

The act seeks more clean fuel from farm and plant sources and more safety for buyers. It seeks leaner use of energy by goods, buildings, and vehicles. It backs study of ways to trap and store greenhouse gases. It also seeks better energy use by the federal government itself. The sample shows Title I, on vehicle fuel economy. It sets higher fleet mileage standards for cars, with a credit trading program and buyer facts. Studies by the National Academy of Sciences are listed too.
plaw-110-141-2007:
Payments to Virginia Tech victims are freed from tax by Public Law 110-141 of 2007. Gross income is not to include sums got from the university out of the Hokie Spirit Memorial Fund.

That fund was set up by the Virginia Tech Foundation, a charity group. The freed sums must be paid on account of the tragic event of April 16, 2007, at the university. In a second, unrelated part, the act raises by one dollar a penalty sum for late partnership tax returns. That change is for tax years that begin in 2008. The act was signed on December 19, 2007.
plaw-110-142-2007:
Forgiven home loan debt gains tax relief in Public Law 110-142, the Mortgage Forgiveness Debt Relief Act of 2007. It amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

A new clause in section 108 frees a discharge of qualified home debt from gross income. The debt must be tied to the taxpayer's main home and be discharged before January 1, 2010. The freed sum must cut the home's tax basis, but not below zero. Qualified debt means debt taken on to buy the home, with limits of two million dollars, or one million for some filers. The sample ends inside a carve-out clause.
plaw-110-143-2007:
Cleanup of closed meth labs is studied under Public Law 110-143, the Methamphetamine Remediation Research Act of 2007. It sets up a research program for making such sites safe again.

Congress found that meth use and making are growing fast across the country. Leftovers from making the drug pose new harms where labs have closed. There is little standard way to tell when a site is truly clean. First cleanups take out only goods that threaten health at once. Strong traces are often found all through homes where labs ran, the findings say. Data and cleanup standards are thin, and states are struggling to set fair rules. The act then orders set guide rules from the environment agency.
plaw-110-144-2007:
Paired organ gifts are freed from crime penalties by Public Law 110-144, the Charlie W. Norwood Living Organ Donation Act of 2007. It amends the National Organ Transplant Act.

Section 301 of that act bans taking organs for gain. The new words state that the ban does not apply to paired donation. In such a swap, a donor wishes to give to one patient but the match fails on body grounds. A second donor and patient are in the same bind. Each donor then gives to the other pair's patient, where the match works. More pairs may join the chain on the same terms.
plaw-110-145-2007: Green Bay, Wisconsin, has the veterans clinic named by Public Law 110-145 of 2007. It is named the Milo C. Huempfner Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic. Any mention of the clinic in a federal law, rule, map, paper, or record is to use that name. The bill passed the House on October 23, 2007, and the Senate on December 13, and was signed on December 21.
plaw-110-146-2007: Miami names its courthouse in Public Law 110-146 of 2007. The courthouse at 301 North Miami Avenue is named the C. Clyde Atkins United States Courthouse. Any mention of the courthouse in a federal law, map, rule, paper, or record is to use that name. The bill passed the House on October 29, 2007, and was signed on December 21.
plaw-110-147-2007: Some vending machines win a break from a dollar coin rule in Public Law 110-147 of 2007. It rewrites part of section 5112 of title 31 of the federal code. Federal bodies whose work uses coins or bills must be able to take one dollar coins. They must also give them out, with one carve-out. Vending machines that take no bills higher than one dollar need not give out dollar coins. The act was signed on December 21, 2007.
plaw-110-148-2007: Approved on December 21, 2007, Public Law 110-148 makes two small edits to the Arizona Water Settlements Act. The 110th Congress changed wording in section 302, which deals with the statement of findings. One edit cuts the text after the word proceedings in one part. The other changes a cross reference from subsection (a) to subsection (b). Nothing else is changed in the text shown.
plaw-110-149-2007:
Public Law 110-149 is a joint resolution from the 110th Congress, approved on December 21, 2007. It made further stopgap funding changes for the fiscal year 2008. The measure amended Public Law 110-92, an earlier stopgap law that was already in force.

The text moves a key date in that earlier law to December 31, 2007. It also adds three new parts. One pays $165,200 to the heirs of Julia Carson, a late House member from Indiana. The other two keep two veterans care and burial powers in force through September 30, 2008. It served as a short bridge while the full yearly bills were finished.
plaw-110-15-2007: At 400 Maryland Avenue Southwest in Washington, the main education building gained a new name under Public Law 110-15. Approved on March 23, 2007, the act calls it the Lyndon Baines Johnson Department of Education Building. Any mention of that building in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the building under its new name.
plaw-110-150-2007:
Extending a special stamp that raises funds for breast cancer research is the work of Public Law 110-150. The 110th Congress approved it on December 21, 2007. The act amended title 39 of the United States Code, the part that covers the Postal Service.

The act changes one year in the law, from 2007 to 2011, so the Postal Service can keep issuing the stamp. It also adds a reporting duty. Health and defense officials must each send Congress a yearly report on funds they got from the stamp. Each report must note key gains or results that those funds helped pay for.
plaw-110-151-2007:
Genocide cases in United States courts are the subject of Public Law 110-151, the Genocide Accountability Act of 2007. Congress approved it on December 21, 2007. The act amended section 1091 of title 18, the federal criminal code.

The change sets when a genocide case may go forward. The act lists five links to this country. The crime took place here in whole or in part, or the accused is a United States national. A case may also rest on lawful home here, or on the accused being brought here after the act, even if the crime took place abroad.
plaw-110-152-2007: In Tiffin, Ohio, the post office at 175 South Monroe Street took a new name under Public Law 110-152. Approved on December 21, 2007, the act calls the site the Paul E. Gillmor Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the site under its new name.
plaw-110-153-2007:
Fixing small errors in the main federal student aid law is the aim of Public Law 110-153. The 110th Congress approved it on December 21, 2007. The act made what its title calls technical corrections to the Higher Education Act of 1965.

One fix spells out what untaxed income and benefits do not include, such as welfare aid and some tax credits. A second fix covers married borrowers who file tax returns apart from a spouse. Their income based loan payments rest on their own debt and income alone. The sample shown here cuts off partway through a third set of fixes, on TEACH grants.
plaw-110-154-2007:
Renaming a major child health institute is the act done by Public Law 110-154, approved on December 21, 2007. The National Institute of Child Health and Human Development became the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development.

Before the rename, the act praises the institute at length. Congress notes it was set up in 1962 at the request of President John F. Kennedy. The findings credit it with cuts in sudden infant death and infant deaths, work on a key vaccine, and training for many child health researchers. The findings add that its trained researchers have aided child health around the world.
plaw-110-155-2007: Patricia Q. Stonesifer of Washington kept her seat on the Smithsonian board under Public Law 110-155. The joint resolution, approved on December 21, 2007, filled a vacancy in the group of regents who are not members of Congress. Her new term runs six years. It took effect on December 22, 2007, the day after approval.
plaw-110-156-2007: Tulsa, Oklahoma gained a renamed veterans clinic under Public Law 110-156, approved on December 26, 2007. The act calls the site the Ernest Childers Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic. Any mention of that clinic in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the clinic under its new name.
plaw-110-157-2007:
Veterans with poor vision are the focus of Public Law 110-157, the Dr. James Allen Veteran Vision Equity Act of 2007. Congress approved it on December 26, 2007. The act amended title 38, the part of the code on veterans benefits.

Its first title changes how vision loss is rated for disability pay, with a fix for cases where both eyes are harmed. A second title covers grave markers, medallions for private markers, and state aid for burials. A third title covers income checks and extends a work study aid program, per the contents list shown.
plaw-110-158-2007: Downtown Des Moines has a renamed federal building under Public Law 110-158, approved on December 26, 2007. The building at 210 Walnut Street in Iowa is now the Neal Smith Federal Building. Any mention of that building in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the building under its new name.
plaw-110-159-2007: Pine Bluff, Arkansas gained a renamed courthouse under Public Law 110-159, approved on December 26, 2007. The building at 100 East 8th Avenue is now the George Howard, Jr. Federal Building and United States Courthouse. Any mention of it in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the building under its new name.
plaw-110-16-2007:
Building a connector road in St. Louis County, Missouri is allowed by Public Law 110-16, approved on March 28, 2007. The project is a short part of arterial road 1151, known as the Lemay Connector Road. The part at issue covers about 0.3 acres of land with limits on its use.

The act lets the county build and run the road on that land despite the limits in two federal laws. In return, the county must guard against added flood harm. It must also set aside a nearby parcel of the same size or larger for open space, recreation, or wetland use.
plaw-110-160-2007:
Keeping a federal terrorism insurance backstop in place is the job of Public Law 110-160, approved on December 26, 2007. Its short title is the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act of 2007. The program sits in the Treasury Department.

The act moves the end date of the 2002 program from 2007 to 2014. It also widens the term act of terrorism, by dropping words that tied it to acts done for a foreign person or interest. The contents list adds a yearly cap on total liability and stronger reports to Congress. The added text lists program years by name through the final year.
plaw-110-161-2007:
Funding much of the federal government for one year is the scale of Public Law 110-161, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2008. Congress approved this large spending law on December 26, 2007. It covers the fiscal year ending September 30, 2008.

The contents list splits the act into many parts, one for each broad area of government. Early parts cover farm programs, rural aid, and the Food and Drug Administration. Later parts cover trade, justice, and science agencies. The act also names the State Department and foreign aid in its opening statement of purpose. Each part sets funds and rules for the agencies under its heading.
plaw-110-162-2007: Hinesville, Georgia has a renamed post office under Public Law 110-162, approved on December 26, 2007. The site at 744 West Oglethorpe Highway is now the John Sidney 'Sid' Flowers Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the site under its new name.
plaw-110-163-2007: Fontana, California gained a renamed post office under Public Law 110-163, approved on December 26, 2007. The site at 16731 Santa Ana Avenue is now the Beatrice E. Watson Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the site under its new name.
plaw-110-164-2007: Who may lead the Office of Compliance is changed by Public Law 110-164, approved on December 26, 2007. Past staff of the office may now serve as its head, deputy head, or general counsel. The act also lets people in those posts serve up to two terms, not just one. That term change covers only people first named to a post after the act took effect.
plaw-110-165-2007: Round Rock, Texas has a renamed post office under Public Law 110-165, approved on December 26, 2007. The site at 797 Sam Bass Road is now the Marine Corps Corporal Steven P. Gill Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the site under its new name.
plaw-110-166-2007:
Relief from the alternative minimum tax for 2007 is the core of Public Law 110-166, the Tax Increase Prevention Act of 2007. Congress approved it on December 26, 2007. The act amended the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

The opening parts raise the amount of income kept free from that tax for tax years that began in 2007. They also extend relief that lets some personal tax credits count against the tax through 2007. The sample shown here cuts off in the third section, so later parts of the act are not described here. The first change applies to tax years beginning after the end of 2006.
plaw-110-167-2007: Lapeer, Michigan gained a renamed post office under Public Law 110-167, approved on December 26, 2007. The site at 567 West Nepessing Street is now the Turrill Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the site under its new name.
plaw-110-168-2007: Modern wards at the veterans medical center in Atlanta, Georgia are funded in principle by Public Law 110-168. Approved on December 26, 2007, the act lets the Secretary of Veterans Affairs carry out a major project to update the inpatient wards there. The cost may not pass $20,534,000. That single grant of power is the whole act.
plaw-110-169-2007: Hillsborough, New Hampshire has a renamed post office under Public Law 110-169, approved on December 26, 2007. The site at 11 Central Street is now the Officer Jeremy Todd Charron Post Office. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record now counts as a mention of the site under its new name. Its own section heading adds the word Building, which the main name does not use.
plaw-110-17-2007:
Backing a larger NATO is the stated aim of Public Law 110-17, the NATO Freedom Consolidation Act of 2007. Congress approved it on April 9, 2007. The act backs timely admission of new members to the alliance.

The findings say NATO's shared defense made the shift to democracy in Central and Eastern Europe possible. They say lasting safety in Europe needs new democracies tied into its main groups. They also cite threats from terror groups and the spread of weapons of mass destruction. The sample cuts off in the findings, before the act's later steps.
plaw-110-170-2007:
Surplus chimpanzees in a federal sanctuary system are protected by Public Law 110-170, the Chimp Haven is Home Act. Congress approved it on December 26, 2007. The act amended the Public Health Service Act.

The change ends the power to remove a chimpanzee from the sanctuary system for research use. One narrow use stays. A chimpanzee may still be used for studies of behavior that do not invade the body, in the act's own words. The law also fixes a numbering clash in the same part of the health act. The short title ties that promise to Chimp Haven by name.
plaw-110-171-2007:
Cross border help in a disaster is cleared by Public Law 110-171, approved on December 26, 2007. The joint resolution gives the consent of Congress to a deal already made. The parties are six New England states and five Canadian provinces.

The states are Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and Connecticut. The provinces are Quebec, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, and Newfoundland. Under the deal, each side may aid the other when asked, after a natural disaster, a hazard, or a civil emergency. The deal also covers joint planning, drills, and training.
plaw-110-172-2007:
Correcting the tax code without changing its policy is the task of Public Law 110-172, the Tax Technical Corrections Act of 2007. Congress approved it on December 29, 2007. The act amended the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

The contents list ties each part to an older tax law that needs a fix. The laws named run from a 1998 act on the tax agency to the Tax Relief and Health Care Act of 2006. Other parts cover pension, energy, transport, and jobs laws. A last part makes plain clerical corrections. The act states that its changes are made to that code unless it says otherwise.
plaw-110-173-2007:
Three big health programs get more time under Public Law 110-173, the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Extension Act of 2007. Congress approved it on December 29, 2007. The act amended titles XVIII, XIX, and XXI of the Social Security Act.

The Medicare title shown in the contents list extends a string of payment rules. They cover a raise in doctor payments, a doctor quality reporting system, and bonus pay in areas short of doctors. Other items cover lab tests in rural areas, therapy cap relief, and plans for people with special needs. The sample ends within that Medicare list.
plaw-110-174-2007:
Pulling public money out of firms that do business in Sudan is backed by Public Law 110-174. Its short title is the Sudan Accountability and Divestment Act of 2007. Congress approved it on December 31, 2007.

The act lets state and local governments sell off assets in such firms. It also bars United States government contracts with them, per the purpose line at its head. Long opening definitions spell out terms such as business operations, which means trade of any kind in Sudan. They also name the government in Khartoum that the act targets.
plaw-110-175-2007:
Open records get a boost from Public Law 110-175, the OPEN Government Act of 2007. Congress approved it on December 31, 2007. The act strengthens the Freedom of Information Act, the 1966 law that lets people seek agency records.

The findings say self government rests on the consent of the governed, and that consent must be informed. They cite court rulings that back a strong bias in favor of giving records out. In the act's quoted words, disclosure, not secrecy, is the chief aim of the records law. The sample shown here covers the findings in depth.
plaw-110-18-2007:
Screening for breast and cervical cancer gets rule changes in Public Law 110-18, approved on April 20, 2007. Its short title is the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program Reauthorization Act of 2007. The act amended the Public Health Service Act.

One change moves a program goal year from 2000 to 2020. The larger change lets the Secretary waive some fund split rules for up to five states, as a test project. A state must use the waiver to draw in non federal funds, and the strict split must be shown to block women from joining.
plaw-110-19-2007: Meals aid for older people is restored in part by Public Law 110-19, the Older Americans Reauthorization Technical Corrections Act. Approved on April 23, 2007, the act reinstates parts of the Older Americans Act of 1965 on the nutrition services incentive program. State agencies and title VI grantees may use their allotments to obtain food goods from farm programs. The farm chief reports how much each group chose in goods. The lead Secretary then moves funds to cover those goods and pays any balance left.
plaw-110-2-2007: Who sits on the board that oversees House pages is recast by Public Law 110-2, the House Page Board Revision Act of 2007. Approved on February 2, 2007, the act aims to equal the seats held by the two parties. It also adds seats for voices outside the House itself. One new member must be a parent of a page, now or within the past five years. A second new member must be a former House page. The board's House seats also grow, from one member named in the old text to two.
plaw-110-20-2007: Memphis gains a second name on a federal building under Public Law 110-20, approved on May 2, 2007. The building at 167 North Main Street in Tennessee was known as the Clifford Davis Federal Building. It is redesignated the Clifford Davis and Odell Horton Federal Building. From then on, federal records that mention that building are read as using the longer, two name form.
plaw-110-21-2007: Advice on how America presents itself abroad keeps its panel under Public Law 110-21, approved on May 2, 2007. The act renews the United States Advisory Commission on Public Diplomacy. It does so with a single date change in the Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act of 1998. The date October 1, 2006 becomes October 1, 2009. That swap is the whole law.
plaw-110-22-2007:
Tougher penalties for animal fighting come from Public Law 110-22, the Animal Fighting Prohibition Enforcement Act of 2007. Congress approved it on May 3, 2007. The act adds a new section to chapter 3 of title 18, the criminal code.

A person who breaks the animal fighting bans in the Animal Welfare Act faces a fine, up to three years in prison, or both, for each breach. The act also bars the sale or transport, across state or national lines, of a knife, gaff, or other sharp tool made to fit a bird's leg for use in a fight. The sample ends inside further wording changes.
plaw-110-23-2007:
Trauma care systems get federal planning duties under Public Law 110-23, approved on May 3, 2007. Its short title is the Trauma Care Systems Planning and Development Act of 2007. The act adds rules on trauma care to the Public Health Service Act.

The health chief must conduct and support research, training, reviews, and demo projects on trauma care. The chief must also help build modern care systems by sharing news among agencies and workers. State and local results, good and bad, are to be gathered and spread, with a special focus on rural needs. Grants and deals may fund the work.
plaw-110-24-2007:
Keeping parts of judges' money records secret for safety is extended by Public Law 110-24, the Judicial Disclosure Responsibility Act. Congress approved it on May 3, 2007. The act amended the Ethics in Government Act of 1978.

The power to hold back a report now covers harm to a family member, not just the judge or court worker. The end year for that power moves from 2005 to 2009. Yearly reports must also add new items. They cover what kind of facts were blacked out, steps that let court parties still spot a conflict, and any public complaints.
plaw-110-25-2007: Duluth gains a long new name for its main federal building under Public Law 110-25. Approved on May 8, 2007, the act covers the building at 515 West First Street in Minnesota. It houses a federal building, a courthouse, and a customhouse in one. All three parts now carry the name Gerald W. Heaney. Later mentions of the site in federal laws, maps, and records are read as mentions under the Heaney name.
plaw-110-26-2007:
Running the American Red Cross in a modern way is the aim of Public Law 110-26, approved on May 11, 2007. Its long name is The American National Red Cross Governance Modernization Act of 2007. The act amends the group's congressional charter.

The findings note the charter had no deep change since 1947. In 2006 the board hired an outside review of its size, role, and ties to managers and local units. A report that fall urged changes to the charter and bylaws. Congress calls a leaner structure a national need. It also wants the board set clearly as a planning and oversight body. The sample ends in the findings.
plaw-110-27-2007: Riverside, California honors a lieutenant in Public Law 110-27, approved on May 25, 2007. The post office at 5757 Tilton Avenue is designated the Lieutenant Todd Jason Bryant Post Office. Under the act, any later mention of that site in a federal law, map, or record counts as a mention of the Bryant post office by name.
plaw-110-28-2007:
War funds, storm recovery, and a wage rise share one large act, Public Law 110-28. Approved on May 25, 2007, it is the U.S. Troop Readiness, Veterans' Care, Katrina Recovery, and Iraq Accountability Appropriations Act, 2007. It makes emergency extra spending for the year ending September 30, 2007.

The contents list runs to ten titles. Early titles fund defense, foreign affairs, and other security needs, plus recovery from Hurricane Katrina. Later titles cover other emergency spending and general rules. Health titles end a children's health funding gap. One title pairs a fair minimum wage with tax relief, and one aids farms.
plaw-110-29-2007: Mayaguez names a post office building in Public Law 110-29, approved on June 1, 2007. The Postal Service site at 60 Calle McKinley, West in Puerto Rico is designated the Miguel Angel Garcia Mendez Post Office Building. Any later mention of that site in a federal law, map, or record is deemed a mention of the building under the Garcia Mendez name.
plaw-110-3-2007: A deadline tied to an older coin era law is reset by Public Law 110-3, approved on February 8, 2007. The act gives a new effective date for how some parts of law apply to Public Law 105-331. For that law's purposes, a two year period in the coin part of title 31 ends on July 1, 2007. The rule applies on and after December 31, 2006, as if it had been enacted on that date. The act is a single short paragraph.
plaw-110-30-2007: Rio Grande City, Texas names a post office in Public Law 110-30, approved on June 1, 2007. The Postal Service site at 500 West Eisenhower Street is designated the Lino Perez, Jr. Post Office. The act's second part deems later mentions of that site, in federal laws and records, to be mentions of the Perez post office by name.
plaw-110-31-2007: Baldwin Park, California names a post office in Public Law 110-31, approved on June 1, 2007. The Postal Service site at 4230 Maine Avenue is designated the Atanacio Haro-Marin Post Office. The title prints the name with a space after the hyphen, while the text prints it closed. Later federal mentions of the site count as mentions under the Haro-Marin name.
plaw-110-32-2007: Lecanto, Florida honors a sergeant in Public Law 110-32, approved on June 1, 2007. The post office at 320 South Lecanto Highway is designated the Sergeant Dennis J. Flanagan Lecanto Post Office Building. Later mentions of that site in federal laws, maps, and records are read as mentions of the building by the Flanagan name.
plaw-110-33-2007: The capital's charter is lined up with its council's school changes by Public Law 110-33. Approved on June 1, 2007, the act amends the District of Columbia Home Rule Act. It strikes two sections of that act whole, sections 452 and 495. It also strikes the matching lines in the act's contents list. The title states the aim, to conform the charter to revisions the Council made on public education. Nothing else is done by the brief text.
plaw-110-34-2007: Interim federal prosecutors are put on a short clock by Public Law 110-34, approved on June 14, 2007. It is the Preserving United States Attorney Independence Act of 2007. A person named by the Attorney General to fill a gap serves only until a set end. That end is the start of a president named United States attorney, or one hundred twenty days, whichever comes first. If the clock runs out, the district court may name a stand-in to serve until the post is filled.
plaw-110-35-2007: Paper filings for housing partners are kept open by Public Law 110-35, approved on June 15, 2007. It is the Preservation Approval Process Improvement Act of 2007. The housing chief must pause a required online filing system for past record forms. Paper forms stay allowed until draft rules are revised to cut needless burdens, and sent to two panels of Congress for review. All filing duties in that process stop at once for a set class. The class is company investors in low income housing tax credit deals.
plaw-110-36-2007: More translators from two wars may enter as special immigrants under Public Law 110-36, approved on June 15, 2007. The act raises the yearly cap in a 2006 defense law for Iraqi and Afghani translators and interpreters. For fiscal years 2007 and 2008, the cap rises from fifty to five hundred. In any other year it stays at fifty. The text also widens who may vouch for such a worker, adding the Chief of Mission. Such entrants are not counted against job based entry limits.
plaw-110-37-2007: Home loans for Native Americans are renewed by Public Law 110-37, approved on June 18, 2007. It is the Native American Home Ownership Opportunity Act of 2007. The act renews the housing chief's program of loan guarantees for Indian housing. It does so with two date swaps in a 1992 housing law. A cap on total loans and a funding grant both move. Their span, fiscal years 1997 through 2007, becomes fiscal years 2008 through 2012.
plaw-110-38-2007: One board seat rule changes under this short act. Public Law 110-38, from the 110th Congress in 2007, makes one small change to board membership rules. It amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1969 so the United States Executive Director of the Inter-American Development Bank may serve on the Board of Directors of the Inter-American Foundation. The Alternate Executive Director may also serve. The change puts those bank officers among the people who can fill three board seats drawn from staff tied to inter-American affairs.
plaw-110-39-2007: Senate child care funding is the narrow subject of Public Law 110-39, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007. The act lets the Secretary of the Senate move money from the Senate Gift Shop Revolving Fund to the Senate Employee Child Care Center. The money must come from sales of holiday ornaments by the Senate Gift Shop. It may fund center needs such as scholarships, learning supplies, and equipment.
plaw-110-4-2007: Public Law 110-4, passed by the 110th Congress in early 2007, gives small business programs more time. It extends programs under the Small Business Act and the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 through July 31, 2007. The act does this by swapping the date February 2, 2007 for July 31, 2007 in an earlier extension law. The change takes effect on February 2, 2007, so the programs do not lapse.
plaw-110-40-2007: Old Virgin Islands laws are repealed by Public Law 110-40, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007. The act repeals sections 1 through 6 of the Act of May 26, 1936, which dealt with the Virgin Islands. The repeal counts as having taken effect on July 22, 1954, long before the 2007 act itself passed. That backdated date is the notable point of this short law.
plaw-110-41-2007:
Public Law 110-41 carries the name Army Specialist Joseph P. Micks Federal Flag Code Amendment Act of 2007. The 110th Congress amended title 4 to let state leaders honor fallen service members from their own state.

The act lets the Governor of a state, territory, or possession order the national flag flown at half-staff there. The honor applies when a member of the Armed Forces from that place dies while on active duty. Congress finds that service members defend the freedom and safety of the United States. The flag honor is ordered by proclamation under the amended text.
plaw-110-42-2007:
Trade benefits for Andean nations are kept alive by Public Law 110-42, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007. It extends the authorities of the Andean Trade Preference Act until February 29, 2008.

The act swaps the end date June 30, 2007 for the new 2008 date. It also repeals the conditional extension rules in the same section. A second part deals with how certain apparel goods are treated under the trade program. It lengthens the run of yearly periods for those goods from four to five. Trade terms for clothing goods often drive talks in such programs.
plaw-110-43-2007: An Illinois post office honors a doctor of the old age pension fight. Public Law 110-43, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007, names one post office building in Fairbury, Illinois. The Postal Service site at 127 East Locust Street shall be known as the Dr. Francis Townsend Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-44-2007: Public Law 110-44 is the First Higher Education Extension Act of 2007, from the 110th Congress. It gives programs under the Higher Education Act of 1965 a short added span of time. The act swaps the date June 30, 2007 for July 31, 2007 in an earlier extension law. It also says the act does not limit or change funding approvals or program spans set by the Higher Education Reconciliation Act of 2005.
plaw-110-45-2007: A New Mexico medical center gains a new name. Public Law 110-45, from the 110th Congress in 2007, renames one federal building in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The building at 1501 San Pedro Drive, SE, long known as the Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, shall be known as the Raymond G. Murphy Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center. Any mention of that building in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-46-2007: Public Law 110-46, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007, names one courthouse in Fresno, California. The United States courthouse bordered by O Street, P Street, Tulare Street, and Capitol Street shall be known as the Robert E. Coyle United States Courthouse. Any mention of that courthouse in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-47-2007:
Public Law 110-47 is the Grand Teton National Park Extension Act of 2007, from the 110th Congress. It changes the bounds of Grand Teton National Park to take in land in the GT Park Subdivision.

The act defines the subdivision as about 49.67 acres. It is shown on a plat filed with the Teton County Clerk and Recorder on December 16, 1997, and on a map of the proposed boundary change. The Secretary in the act means the Secretary of the Interior. Park means Grand Teton National Park itself. Land next to a park can shape views, wildlife paths, and water flow.
plaw-110-48-2007:
Public Law 110-48, from the 110th Congress in 2007, extends two health programs through the end of fiscal year 2007. The programs are transitional medical assistance, called TMA, and the abstinence education program.

The act edits an earlier tax and health law by changing June 30 to September 30. It also swaps third quarter for fourth quarter where those words appear. A second part ends a limited continuous enrollment rule for certain Medicare Advantage members. A third part makes an offsetting change in the Medicare Advantage Stabilization Fund. Three extra months kept both programs from lapsing at mid-year.
plaw-110-49-2007:
Public Law 110-49 is the Foreign Investment and National Security Act of 2007. The 110th Congress sought to guard national safety while still welcoming foreign investment and the jobs it brings.

The act reforms how such deals are checked for harm to national safety. It sets up in law the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States. It also adds factors to weigh in a review and covers deals after they close, with tracking and enforcement. Congress gains a stronger oversight role under the act. The review body weighs jobs and growth against safety risks.
plaw-110-5-2007:
Public Law 110-5 is the Revised Continuing Appropriations Resolution, 2007, a joint resolution of the 110th Congress. It makes further continuing funds for fiscal year 2007, keeping the government funded.

The resolution rewrites the earlier Continuing Appropriations Resolution, 2007 in full. Division B then lists the sums provided, drawn from the Treasury and other funds. The money goes to the departments, agencies, and other units of government for that fiscal year. Title I covers full-year continuing funding at set levels for the work named. Continuing acts are stopgaps used when yearly bills are not yet done.
plaw-110-50-2007:
Public Law 110-50, the Passport Backlog Reduction Act of 2007, helps the Department of State face a sharp lack of passport staff. The 110th Congress let the department bring back retired workers for the task.

The act amends the Foreign Service Act of 1980 on rehiring retired Foreign Service staff. Rehired staff may help consular posts with a large backlog of visa cases. They may also help meet demand from new passport and travel document rules. The goal is to clear long waits for travel papers. Travel rules that year drove a surge in passport demand nationwide.
plaw-110-51-2007: Public Law 110-51 is the Second Higher Education Extension Act of 2007, from the 110th Congress. Like the first extension that year, it gives programs under the Higher Education Act of 1965 more time. The act swaps July 31, 2007 for October 31, 2007 in the 2005 extension law. It also says the act does not limit funding approvals or program spans set by the Higher Education Reconciliation Act of 2005.
plaw-110-52-2007: Public Law 110-52 is a joint resolution of the 110th Congress approving the renewal of import limits in the Burmese Freedom and Democracy Act of 2003. Congress approves the renewal of the limits in section 3(a)(1) of that act. The resolution also moves a merchandise fee date from October 14, 2014 to October 21, 2014. A further part shifts the rate for payment of company estimated taxes from 114.50 percent to 114.75 percent.
plaw-110-53-2007:
Public Law 110-53 carries the title Implementing Recommendations of the 9/11 Commission Act of 2007. The 110th Congress wrote it to put into effect the advice of the National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States.

Title I covers homeland security grants, including the Homeland Security Grant Program. It also amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 and a post-Katrina emergency management law. Title II covers grants for emergency management performance. Grants for building emergency operations centers are part of that title. Grants for emergency operations centers sit in that same title.
plaw-110-54-2007: Doctors called to duty gain a billing exception. Public Law 110-54, from the 110th Congress in 2007, amends title XVIII of the Social Security Act on Medicare billing. It creates an exception to the 60-day limit on shared billing deals between two doctors. The exception applies when one doctor is ordered to active duty as a member of a reserve force. Before January 1, 2008, the stand-in billing may run for a longer stretch, for the whole time the first doctor serves on that duty.
plaw-110-55-2007:
Public Law 110-55 is the Protect America Act of 2007. The 110th Congress amended the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 to add steps for approving certain gathering of foreign intelligence facts.

A new section 105A states a key limit on the law's reach. The meaning of electronic surveillance shall not be read to cover spying aimed at a person thought to be outside the United States. Further new text adds more steps for approving that kind of gathering. The act drew wide debate over privacy and safety. New section numbers in the older act carry the added steps.
plaw-110-56-2007:
Emergency bridge aid for Minneapolis is provided by Public Law 110-56, passed by the 110th Congress in August 2007. The Interstate I-35W bridge there fell on August 1, 2007, and the act funds its repair and rebuilding.

The Secretary of Transportation may carry out the repair project, and the federal share of the cost is 100 percent. The act clears 250 million dollars for the work, to stay open until spent. It also waives the 100 million dollar cap on emergency relief funds for this project. Transit and travel facts services gain wider use as well.
plaw-110-57-2007: Small business programs gain four and a half more months. Public Law 110-57, from the 110th Congress in 2007, gives small business programs another short extension. It extends programs under the Small Business Act and the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 through December 15, 2007. The act swaps July 31, 2007 for December 15, 2007 in the earlier extension law, as already changed once that year. The change takes effect on July 31, 2007, so no gap opens in the programs.
plaw-110-58-2007: In Harrison, Tennessee, the post office at 6301 Highway 58 gains a new name under Public Law 110-58, enacted by the 110th Congress in 2007. From then on the Postal Service site is called the Claude Ramsey Post Office. Federal laws, maps, and records that name the site are read as naming the Claude Ramsey Post Office instead.
plaw-110-59-2007: Seneca, South Carolina is home to the post office renamed by Public Law 110-59, a 2007 act of the 110th Congress. The building at 508 East Main Street becomes the S/Sgt Lewis G. Watkins Post Office Building. Under the act, any federal mention of that site in a law, map, or record means the new name.
plaw-110-6-2007: Public Law 110-6, the Antitrust Modernization Commission Extension Act of 2007, gives one study body more time. The act amends the Antitrust Modernization Commission Act of 2002 to extend the term of the Commission. It changes 30 days to 60 days in the end-date rule. It also makes a small fix, swapping a wrong section cite for section 11058. The Commission studied whether antitrust laws needed updating.
plaw-110-60-2007: Bakersfield, California gains a renamed post office under Public Law 110-60, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007. The Postal Service site at 118 Minner Avenue is designated the Buck Owens Post Office. References to that site in any United States law, map, or record are treated as references to the Buck Owens Post Office.
plaw-110-61-2007: Under Public Law 110-61, a 2007 law of the 110th Congress, the post office at 4551 East 52nd Street in Odessa, Texas takes a new name. It is designated the Staff Sergeant Marvin 'Rex' Young Post Office Building. Any mention of the site in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of that name.
plaw-110-62-2007: Public Law 110-62 renames the Postal Service building at 896 Pittsburgh Street in Springdale, Pennsylvania. Enacted in 2007 by the 110th Congress, the act designates the site as the Rachel Carson Post Office Building. Later federal records that point to the building point to it under the Carson name. The honored name is Rachel Carson, as the act's heading states.
plaw-110-63-2007: University City, Missouri is the setting for Public Law 110-63, a postal naming act from the 110th Congress in 2007. The site at 561 Kingsland Avenue shall be known as the Harriett F. Woods Post Office Building. The act adds the standard rule: mentions of the site in laws, maps, and federal records mean the new name.
plaw-110-64-2007: Public Law 110-64, enacted in 2007, gives the post office at 601 Banyan Trail in Boca Raton, Florida a person's name. The building becomes the Leonard W. Herman Post Office. As with like acts, a mention of the site in a United States law, map, or other record is deemed a mention of the Herman name.
plaw-110-65-2007: Chicago, Illinois gains the Willye B. White Post Office Building under Public Law 110-65, a 2007 act of the 110th Congress. The honored site stands at 11033 South State Street. The act states that references to that Postal Service site in federal laws, maps, and records shall be read as references to the new building name.
plaw-110-66-2007: In Blue Creek, Ohio, Public Law 110-66 names the post office building at 20805 State Route 125. Passed in 2007, the act calls the site the George B. Lewis Post Office Building. Federal maps, laws, and records that name the site now name it under the Lewis title. The site stands on State Route 125, as the act states.
plaw-110-67-2007: Public Law 110-67 designates the post office at 14536 State Route 136 in Cherry Fork, Ohio. The 110th Congress acted in 2007 to name the site the Staff Sergeant Omer 'O.T.' Hawkins Post Office. A reference to the site in any law, map, or federal record is a reference to the Hawkins name under the act.
plaw-110-68-2007: Chelsea, Oklahoma is home to the building renamed by Public Law 110-68 in 2007. The Postal Service site at 408 West 6th Street becomes the Clem Rogers McSpadden Post Office Building. The act provides that mentions of the site in United States laws, maps, and records count as mentions of the new name.
plaw-110-69-2007:
Public Law 110-69 is the America COMPETES Act, also read as the America Creating Opportunities to Meaningfully Promote Excellence in Technology, Education, and Science Act. The 110th Congress passed it in 2007 to invest in new ideas through research.

The stated aim is to improve how well the United States competes with other nations. Title I covers government-wide science, led by the Office of Science and Technology Policy. It calls for a national science and technology summit and a study of blocks to new ideas. A national medal for technology and new ideas is also covered.
plaw-110-7-2007: Vail, Colorado gains a renamed post office building under Public Law 110-7, an early 2007 act of the 110th Congress. The site at 1300 North Frontage Road West is designated the Gerald R. Ford, Jr. Post Office Building. References to the site in federal laws, maps, and records are deemed references to the Ford name.
plaw-110-70-2007: Public Law 110-70, enacted by the 110th Congress in 2007, names the post office building at 3916 Milgen Road in Columbus, Georgia. It shall be known as the Frank G. Lumpkin, Jr. Post Office Building. Any law, map, or federal record naming that Postal Service site names it under the Lumpkin title after the act.
plaw-110-71-2007: Marshalltown, Iowa is the town in Public Law 110-71, a postal naming act of 2007. The building at 309 East Linn Street becomes the Major Scott Nisely Post Office. The act adds that a mention of that site in a United States law, map, or record is a mention of the Nisely name.
plaw-110-72-2007: Fort Collins, Colorado is home to the building renamed by Public Law 110-72 in 2007. The Postal Service site at 301 Boardwalk Drive becomes the Dr. Karl E. Carson Post Office Building. The act provides that mentions of the site in United States laws, maps, and records count as mentions of the new name.
plaw-110-73-2007: Public Law 110-73 designates the post office at 103 South Getty Street in Uvalde, Texas. The 110th Congress acted in 2007 to name the site the Dolph Briscoe, Jr. Post Office Building. A reference to the site in any law, map, or federal record is a reference to the Briscoe name under the act.
plaw-110-74-2007: Park staff on a border island gain health cover. Public Law 110-74, from the 110th Congress in 2007, amends chapter 89 of title 5 on federal health coverage. It makes staff of the Roosevelt Campobello International Park Commission able to obtain federal health insurance. The edit adds a new group to the list in section 8901: a person employed by the Commission who is a citizen of the United States. That single addition is the whole law.
plaw-110-75-2007:
Public Law 110-75 lets the Coquille Indian Tribe of Oregon deal freely with its own land. The 110th Congress acted in 2007, despite any other law or rule to the contrary.

The Tribe, or its agents, may transfer, lease, encumber, or otherwise convey its stake in real property. No further approval is needed. The freedom covers land that is not held in trust by the United States for the Tribe. The act sets limits in later subsections, and it does not reach deals made before its window. Land the tribe owns in fee is the land this freedom covers.
plaw-110-76-2007:
Like its Oregon twin in the same week, Public Law 110-76 frees a tribe to convey its own land. The 110th Congress acted for the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe of Michigan in 2007.

The Tribe may transfer, lease, encumber, or otherwise convey its stake in real property, with no further approval needed. The power covers land not held in trust by the United States for the Tribe. The act states plainly that nothing in it lets the Tribe convey land that is held in trust. Trust land stays under the older rules, as the act makes clear.
plaw-110-77-2007:
Public Law 110-77, from the 110th Congress in 2007, improves how Idaho uses land granted for an agricultural college. It amends the Act of July 3, 1890, which made the grant.

Despite parts of the First Morrill Act of 1862, Idaho may invest and manage earnings from the granted land. The state must follow the standards that apply to a trustee under Idaho law. Idaho may also deduct trustee-level costs from the earnings. The act then covers how the earnings and proceeds may be used. Trustee standards set how the money must be handled with care.
plaw-110-78-2007:
Public Law 110-78 waives one law for one parcel of land in Oregon. The 110th Congress acted in 2007 for land sent by the United States to two Indian tribes in that state.

The findings tell the parcel's story. The land, about 19.86 acres in Marion County, was once part of the Chemawa Indian School. The United States deeded it in 2002 to the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians and the Confederated Tribes of the Grand Ronde Community. Long before, in 1973 and 1974, the land went to Oregon for highway work on Interstate Route 5 and the Salem Parkway.
plaw-110-79-2007:
Public Law 110-79 gives the consent of Congress to an interstate forest fire pact. The 110th Congress approved the Great Plains Wildland Fire Protection Compact in 2007, and the act prints the pact text in full.

The pact joins state, provincial, and territorial wildland fire agencies as members. Its purpose is to spur strong prevention and control of forest fires in the Great Plains region. Members agree to keep fit forest fire fighting services in place. Shared help across state lines is the core idea behind the deal. Fires cross state lines fast, which is why states join such pacts.
plaw-110-8-2007: Laramie, Wyoming gains a renamed post office under Public Law 110-8, an early 2007 act of the 110th Congress. The site at 152 North 5th Street is designated the Gale W. McGee Post Office. References to the site in federal laws, maps, and records are deemed references to the McGee name. The honored name is Gale W. McGee, as the act's heading states.
plaw-110-80-2007: One section of a war funding act is struck. Public Law 110-80, from the 110th Congress in 2007, strikes one section from a large spending law. The heading in the sample reads Contract Waiver. The act amends the U.S. Troop Readiness, Veterans' Care, Katrina Recovery, and Iraq Accountability Appropriations Act, 2007 by striking section 9012. The catalog title says that section held a requirement tied to forage producers. Striking the section is the whole act.
plaw-110-81-2007:
Public Law 110-81 is the Honest Leadership and Open Government Act of 2007. The 110th Congress wrote it to provide greater openness in how laws are made.

Title I is called Closing the Revolving Door. It tightens limits on former officers, staff, and elected officials of both branches after they leave office. It also bars wrongly swaying a private firm's hiring choices and requires notice of post-job limits. Title II turns to full public disclosure of lobbying, with quarterly filing of lobbying reports. Lobbying reports move to a four-times-a-year pace under Title II.
plaw-110-82-2007:
Public Law 110-82 is the Native American $1 Coin Act, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007. It orders the Secretary of the Treasury to mint and issue coins honoring Native Americans.

The act amends section 5112 of title 31 to add a new coin program. From January 1, 2008, circulating one-dollar coins are redesigned to honor Native Americans. The coins mark the key gifts made by Indian tribes and by single Native Americans to the growth of the United States and its history. One-dollar coins in this program stay in daily use as money.
plaw-110-83-2007:
Public Law 110-83 sets up a youth exchange program between the United States and Poland. The 110th Congress passed the United States-Poland Parliamentary Youth Exchange Program Act of 2007.

The findings trace the two nations' close ties. The United States opened relations with the new Polish Republic in April 1919, and ties have been close since 1989. Poland joined the North Atlantic Treaty Organization in March 1999 and the European Union in May 2004. Poland is praised as a strong backer of United States-led efforts against global terrorism. The exchange pairs young people with a parliament in each nation.
plaw-110-84-2007:
Public Law 110-84 is the College Cost Reduction and Access Act, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007. It provides for budget reconciliation under the fiscal year 2008 budget resolution. Most of its edits land in the Higher Education Act of 1965.

The act takes effect on October 1, 2007, unless a part states a different date. Title I covers grants to students at colleges and other schools of higher learning. Its first section deals with tuition sensitivity in grant rules. The act's name states its twin aims: lower college costs and wider access. Most parts of the act took effect on October 1, 2007.
plaw-110-85-2007:
Public Law 110-85 is the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007. The 110th Congress amended the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act in broad ways.

Title I renews the user-fee program for prescription drugs. It covers the power to assess and use drug fees and fees tied to review of drug ads on television. The act also extends the user-fee program for medical devices. It strengthens the postmarket powers of the Food and Drug Administration on drug safety, after drugs reach the market. User fees are paid by drug and device makers to fund reviews.
plaw-110-86-2007: Locally hired Peace Corps staff gain a pay fund. Public Law 110-86, from the 110th Congress in 2007, lets the Peace Corps pay separation pay to one group of workers. The workers are host country resident personal services contractors of the Peace Corps. The act sets up a fund in the Treasury for that pay. The Director may deposit sums already set aside and sums for fiscal years after 2006. From fiscal year 2007, money in the fund is open for the stated purpose.
plaw-110-87-2007: In New York, New York, the post office at 365 West 125th Street gains a new name under Public Law 110-87, enacted by the 110th Congress in 2007. From then on the Postal Service site is called the Percy Sutton Post Office Building. Federal laws, maps, and records that name the site are read as naming the Percy Sutton Post Office Building instead.
plaw-110-88-2007: Public Law 110-88, a 2007 act of the 110th Congress, names one stretch of highway in Baltimore, Maryland. The part of Interstate Route 395 from the junction with Interstate Route 95 to Conway Street shall be known as Cal Ripken Way. Any mention of that stretch of road in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-89-2007:
Public Law 110-89, from the 110th Congress in 2007, extends the trade adjustment assistance program for three months. The program sits under the Trade Act of 1974 and helps workers, firms, and farmers hurt by trade.

For workers, the act moves a date from September 30, 2007 to December 31, 2007. For firms, it adds four million dollars for the three months starting October 1, 2007. For farmers, it provides nine million dollars to the Department of Agriculture for the same span. A second section covers offsets for the cost. A short bridge of aid keeps help in place while trade talks go on.
plaw-110-9-2007: Little Rock, Arkansas is home to the post office renamed by Public Law 110-9, a 2007 act of the 110th Congress. The building at 1700 Main Street becomes the Scipio A. Jones Post Office Building. Under the act, any federal mention of that site in a law, map, or record means the new name.
plaw-110-90-2007:
Public Law 110-90 bears the name TMA, Abstinence Education, and QI Programs Extension Act of 2007. The 110th Congress extended three health programs in one act.

The act extends transitional medical assistance, called TMA, and the abstinence education program through December 31, 2007. It edits an earlier law by changing September 30 to December 31 and fiscal year 2006 to fiscal year 2007. A third section extends the qualifying individuals program, the QI program, through December 2007 as well. All three aid low-income health coverage or schooling. All three programs are tied to health coverage for low-income people.
plaw-110-91-2007: Public Law 110-91 is a short joint resolution of the 110th Congress raising the legal cap on the public debt. It amends section 3101 of title 31, United States Code. The resolution strikes the old dollar limit in that section and inserts a new one of $9,815,000,000,000. That single swap, raising the debt ceiling to about 9.8 trillion dollars, is the whole resolution.
plaw-110-92-2007:
Public Law 110-92 is a joint resolution making continuing funds for fiscal year 2008. The 110th Congress used it to keep the government running as the new fiscal year began.

The resolution provides sums from the Treasury and other funds for the departments, agencies, and other units of government. Section 101 provides such amounts as may be needed, at the rate set by the fiscal year 2007 funding laws. The money keeps projects and work going that were carried on in 2007 and funded that year. Later sections limit how the funds may be used.
plaw-110-93-2007:
Public Law 110-93 makes one waiver power permanent. The 110th Congress acted on the power of the Secretary of Education over student aid during a war, a military operation, or a national emergency.

Congress states that the Higher Education Relief Opportunities for Students Act of 2003 fits the special cases faced by active duty troops. Those cases touch school enrollment and federal student loans. The sense of Congress is that the 2003 rules should be made permanent. Section 2 then makes that extension of waiver power permanent in law. Permanent power ends the need to renew the waiver rule each crisis.
plaw-110-94-2007:
Public Law 110-94 is the Pesticide Registration Improvement Renewal Act, passed by the 110th Congress in 2007. It amends the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act, the main pesticide law.

The act renews and amends the rules for faster review of covered pesticide products. It clears fees for certain pesticide products and extends and improves the gathering of maintenance fees. Early parts deal with the review of applications, tying review steps to a set timetable. Registration review gets its own part, showing the act's focus on how products gain approval. Fees paid by makers fund the review work the act describes.
plaw-110-95-2007:
Public Law 110-95 awards a congressional gold medal to Michael Ellis DeBakey, M.D. The 110th Congress opened the act with findings on his life and work.

DeBakey was born September 7, 1908, in Lake Charles, Louisiana. At age 23, still a medical student, he reported a key invention, a roller pump for blood transfusions. That pump later became a major part of the heart-lung machine used in the first successful open-heart operation. Though already famed for work on blood vessel disease, he volunteered for service in World War II and rose to Colonel.
plaw-110-96-2007:
Public Law 110-96 is the International Emergency Economic Powers Enhancement Act, from the 110th Congress in 2007. It amends the penalty parts of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

The act rewrites section 206 on penalties. It is unlawful to violate, try to violate, plot to violate, or cause a breach of any license, order, or ban issued under that law. A civil penalty may reach the greater of 250,000 dollars or twice a set base amount. The stiffer fines give the emergency powers law sharper teeth. The penalty must fit the greater-of test the new text sets out.
plaw-110-97-2007:
Public Law 110-97 extends the District of Columbia College Access Act of 1999. The 110th Congress gave the tuition aid programs five more years in 2007.

For both the public school program and the private school program, the act swaps seven succeeding fiscal years for twelve. That change lengthens the run of aid for District students who seek college. A second part adds means testing to the public school program rules. Means testing ties the size of aid to a family's income and need. More years of aid help District students plan a full college course.
plaw-110-98-2007: Bakersfield-style naming comes to New Jersey in Public Law 110-98, a 2007 act of the 110th Congress. In Jersey City, the Postal Service building at 69 Montgomery Street becomes the Frank J. Guarini Post Office Building. Federal laws, maps, and records that name the site are read as naming the Guarini building.
plaw-110-99-2007: Public Law 110-99 renames the Postal Service building at 555 South 3rd Street Lobby in Memphis, Tennessee. Enacted in 2007 by the 110th Congress, the act designates the site as the Kenneth T. Whalum, Sr. Post Office Building. Later federal records that point to the building point to it under the Whalum name.
plos-pbio-0020007:
Howard Y. Chang, Julie B. Sneddon, Ash A. Alizadeh, and a large team linked wound healing to cancer in PLOS Biology in 2004. When skin is cut, fibroblast cells switch on a set of genes to close the wound. Tumors switch on much the same set, which is why cancers are sometimes called wounds that do not heal.

The authors used that gene pattern to sort real tumors. Cancers that showed the wound pattern tended to grow and spread more, and patients fared worse. That makes the pattern a useful warning sign. It also gives doctors a possible tool for judging risk. A gene test based on healing signals could help guide how strongly a cancer should be treated.
plos-pbio-0020207:
Andrew Fortna, Young Kim, Erik MacLaren, and a large team compared gene copies in humans and great apes for PLOS Biology in 2004. Genes can be gained or lost as species split. The team measured copy numbers across the ape family tree to find changes unique to each line.

Human-specific gains and losses stand out as candidate traits that set us apart. Some involve genes tied to the brain and to smell, two areas where humans differ from other apes. A clean list of lineage-specific changes gives evolution research sharp targets. Each entry can be tested for what it does, rather than guessed at from the full genome.
plos-pbio-0030007:
Adam Woolfe, Martin Goodson, Debbie K. Goode, and a large team hunted conserved DNA in PLOS Biology in 2005. Some DNA stretches do not code for proteins yet are nearly identical across vertebrates. Such strong conservation hints they do a vital job, likely guiding development.

The team found these stretches cluster near genes that control how embryos grow. Placed near a gene in a developing fish, many of them acted as switches that turned the gene on in specific tissues. That confirmed the guess: conserved non-coding DNA holds instructions for body building. The catalog became a resource for finding the switches behind birth defects and for reading the genome's dark matter.
plos-pone-0000007:
Casper Breuker, James Patterson, and Christian Klingenberg studied why fruit fly wings come out so reliably the same shape. Development is noisy, yet a Drosophila wing lands close to its target form again and again. That steadiness is called developmental buffering. Their 2006 paper argues the buffering has a single basis.

Working from wing measurements, the team tested whether one shared mechanism damps the many small disturbances that could warp a growing wing. A single basis would simplify a tangle of older theories, each invoking its own buffer. The claim matters beyond flies: reliable development despite noise is a basic problem for every animal, humans included.
plos-pone-0000107:
Marta Martínez-Diez, Gema Santamaría, Álvaro D. Ortega, and their team studied mitochondria across the cell cycle in PLOS ONE in 2006. Mitochondria, the cell's power plants, must be built and split between daughter cells as the cell divides. The team tracked how new mitochondria form and move through that cycle.

They also probed the role of 3′UTRs, the tail regions of gene messages that control where and when proteins are made. Those tails appear to help place mitochondria-making proteins where they are needed. The study links two levels of control: the timetable of division and the fine print on gene messages. Both matter for cells that must double their power supply on schedule.
plos-pone-0000207:
Wayne M. Getz, Scott Fortmann-Roe, Paul C. Cross, and colleagues published this ecology methods paper in PLOS ONE in 2007. It presents LoCoH, a set of nonparametric kernel methods for building home ranges and utilization distributions from animal location data. A home range map estimates where an animal actually spends its time.

Older range methods often drew smooth blobs that included land the animal never used. LoCoH builds ranges from local hulls of points, respecting rivers, fences, and other hard edges. Wildlife researchers adopted such tools widely for tracking data, from collared lions to tagged birds.
plos-pone-0000307:
Tonio Ball, Benjamin Rahm, Simon B. Eickhoff, and colleagues published this brain imaging paper in PLOS ONE in 2007. The amygdala, the brain's alarm center, has subregions with different jobs. The authors combine functional MRI with probabilistic anatomical maps to measure the response properties of human amygdala subregions in living people.

Treating the amygdala as one blob blurs its real organization. Splitting it by anatomy while scanning activity gives a cleaner picture of which part does what. The method helps research on fear, emotion, and anxiety disorders aim at the right subregion.
plos-pone-0000407:
Masaki Fujita, Hisako Takeshita, and Hitoshi Sawa studied how cells know when to stop dividing and specialize, using the worm C. elegans, in PLOS ONE in 2007. Their focus was cyclin E and its partner CDK2, proteins best known for driving cells into division. The team examined cells that had divided unequally and then settled into a resting, quiescent state.

The authors report that cyclin E and CDK2 help hold those resting cells back from finishing their differentiation. That is an unexpected brake role for proteins famous as accelerators. Worm embryos are a classic system for watching single cells choose their fates. The finding adds a twist to how division machinery and specialization are coordinated.
plos-pone-0000507:
Trinh Thanh Thuy and colleagues documented tuberculosis among people with HIV in a Vietnamese province, in a 2007 PLOS ONE paper. TB is the leading killer of people with HIV worldwide, and An Giang Province in 2001–2004 gave the team a defined place and period. They reported the epidemiology of HIV-associated TB there and the outcomes of TB treatment.

Treatment outcomes show whether programs work in practice, not just in trials. In the early 2000s, Vietnam was scaling up both HIV and TB services, and their overlap was poorly documented. Local numbers like these guide where joint TB-HIV care will save the most lives.
plos-pone-0000607:
Christopher L. Reyes and colleagues froze a cell delivery machine at steps of its work cycle, in a 2007 PLOS ONE paper. The machine is the signal recognition particle receptor. It guides new proteins to the cell's surface for export. The team used X-ray methods to solve the receptor's shapes, catching forms it takes mid-job.

The mid-job shapes are the frames between the still pictures in textbooks. They show how the machine truly moves as it works. Protein targeting is basic to all cells, and its parts are targets for drugs that jam bacterial export. Frames like these turn a rough sketch of a pathway into a true plan.
plos-pone-0000707:
Philip Bejon, Edna Ogada, Tabitha Mwangi and colleagues reported extended follow-up of two candidate malaria vaccines tested in Kenyan children.
